content_text:
Applied Materials Raises BE Semiconductor Stake to 20%, Deepening AI Advanced Packaging Push; Deal Awaits U.S. Antitrust Review
Add preferred source 2 
Applied Materials announced it will raise its stake in Dutch packaging equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries from 9% to approximately 20%, having signed an accelerated share purchase agreement, with the deal still pending U.S. antitrust review. Applied Materials became BE Semiconductor's largest shareholder after first taking a stake in April 2025, and the increased holding is aimed at AI chip advanced packaging. The two companies have collaborated on hybrid bonding technology since 2020 and have jointly developed the Kinex integrated die-to-wafer system. Applied Materials said it does not intend to push its stake above 20% or seek board seats. BE Semiconductor holds roughly 70% of the global hybrid bonding equipment market, with third-quarter orders up 96% year over year, and hybrid bonding equipment orders in the first nine months of 2026 already more than double the full-year 2025 level.
Key Elements 
Applied Materials BE Semiconductor Industries hybrid bonding EPIC Center Prabh Raja ASML Kinex Piotech 
U.S. semiconductor equipment giant Applied Materials announced Monday that it will raise its stake in Dutch packaging equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries (BESI) from the current 9% to approximately 20%, deepening cooperation between the two companies in advanced packaging for artificial intelligence (AI) chips. The increased holding has been signed under an accelerated share purchase agreement but still requires U.S. antitrust review.
Applied Materials became the largest shareholder of the Dutch company after first taking a 9% stake in April 2025. At that time, BE Semiconductor had a market value of about $13 billion. Under the plan, the stake will approach 20% once the increase is completed. However, Applied Materials made clear that at this stage it does not intend to push its holding above 20% or seek seats on BE Semiconductor's board, indicating that this is a long-term strategic investment centered on technology cooperation rather than a move toward a full acquisition.
The expanded cooperation focuses on next-generation chip interconnection and packaging technology, with the goal of supporting the next generation of AI semiconductors. The two companies have jointly invested in hybrid bonding process development since 2020, a technology regarded as a key link in advanced packaging and mainly used for high-performance chips.
Hybrid bonding is characterized by directly bonding copper interconnects and dielectric layers without the need for traditional bumps, allowing a substantial increase in connection density between chips. The two companies have jointly developed the Kinex integrated die-to-wafer hybrid bonding system, combining Applied Materials' expertise in etching, planarization, deposition and inspection with BE Semiconductor's technology in high-precision die placement and assembly. BE Semiconductor also recently formally joined Applied Materials' newly established chip equipment research organization, the EPIC Center.
Prabh Raja, president of Applied Materials' Semiconductor Products Group, said in a statement: "We look forward to further deepening our strategic collaboration with Besi to deliver the innovative products and technologies customers need to scale AI systems."
From a market structure perspective, BE Semiconductor holds a critical position in the advanced packaging equipment sector. According to market data, BE Semiconductor accounts for about 70% of the global hybrid bonding equipment market. Its flagship model, the Datacon 8800 CHAMEO ultra plus AC, achieves alignment accuracy of up to 100 nanometers and a throughput of up to 2,000 cycles per hour, with volume production potential.
Demand-side momentum is also strengthening. BE Semiconductor's third-quarter orders surged 96% year over year to €342.6 million (approximately $382.0 million); hybrid bonding equipment orders in the first nine months of 2026 were already more than double the full-year 2025 level. The company's latest financial report shows that its hybrid bonding customer base has expanded to 23 companies, with cumulative equipment demand exceeding 215 units.
It is worth noting that last week the market briefly worried that Dutch semiconductor equipment leader ASML might become a competitor to BE Semiconductor in the hybrid bonding arena, which BE Semiconductor has denied. Against the backdrop of advanced packaging becoming key to the AI chip computing power race, alliances and competitive-cooperative relationships among equipment makers are rapidly intensifying.
On the other hand, Chinese equipment makers are also catching up in hybrid bonding technology. China's Piotech recorded hybrid bonding equipment revenue of CNY 136 million (approximately $20.4 million) in 2025, up 41.92% year over year, and has secured repeat orders for wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding systems, meaning that this niche market previously dominated by a small number of vendors is gradually seeing new suppliers emerge.
For investors, the most direct significance of this deal is that Applied Materials is betting its resources on the "back-end" packaging link of AI chips. As advancing Moore's Law becomes increasingly difficult, improvements in chip performance increasingly depend on advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration, and hybrid bonding is one of the highest-barrier technologies in this area. By tying up with BE Semiconductor through a stake purchase rather than an acquisition, Applied Materials can share technology and customers while avoiding the operational risks and regulatory resistance of full integration.
However, the deal still must pass U.S. antitrust review, and the timetable and conditions remain uncertain. Applied Materials has also stated that it will not pursue board seats or increase its stake further, and whether the cooperation can be translated into substantive orders and revenue contribution will be a key focus for the market going forward.

content_text:
CoTec Holdings Corp. Notes HyProMag USA Pre-Feasibility Study Outlining Future Expansion Options to Quadruple Planned U.S. Rare Earth Magnet Capacity, Indicating an Incremental Post-Tax NPV of Up to US$2.1 billion
Investing News Network 
October 27, 2026 
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / October 27, 2026 / CoTec Holdings Corp. ( TSXV:CTH )(OTCQX:CTHCF) ("CoTec" or the "Company") notes the press release issued yesterday October 26, 2026, by its joint venture, HyProMag USA LLC ("HyProMag USA"), announcing the completion of an independent Pre-Feasibility Study (" PFS " or the "Study") undertaken by PegasusTSI Inc. and BBA USA Inc. evaluating the potential expansion of HyProMag USA's proposed U.S. rare earth magnet manufacturing platform beyond its first plant in Northlake, Texas (the "Northlake Texas Facility"), which is in detailed engineering, with Phase 1 commissioning expected in mid-2028.
CoTec Holdings: HyProMag USA PFS Outlines 4x U.S. Magnet Capacity youtube.com 
The PFS evaluates a three-plant[i] phased expansion strategy: three new regional production plants, supported by a centralized manufacturing, finishing and technology hub (the " Central Texas Hub "), to produce commercial neodymium iron boron ("NdFeB") magnet products in the United States from both end-of-life recycled feedstock and primary alloy material. Together with the Northlake Texas Facility[ii], the platform targets total salable material production of approximately 6,000 metric tons per year by 2034, an increase of 4,474 metric tons per year above production from the Northlake Texas Facility.
Annual total magnetic material production in 2034 from HyProMag USA would comprise approximately 4,192 metric tons of magnets, 1,305 metric tons of magnetic NdFeB alloy powder and 503 metric tons of other salable material. The PFS economics listed below cover the three new plants, including the Central Texas Hub only; they do not include the Northlake Texas Facility, whose value is not included in the PFS results.
The Study builds upon the engineering and development work completed for the Northlake Texas Facility and outlines a pathway for HyProMag USA to develop from a Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap ("HPMS")[iii] enabled magnet recycler into a fully integrated producer of commercial rare earth magnet products for U.S. customers.
HyProMag USA believes the platform combines the cost advantages and operational flexibility of both end-of-life recycled feedstock and primary alloy feedstocks, providing a flexible and scalable pathway to magnet manufacturing.
HyProMag USA may also benefit from potential future access to primary sourced feedstock from Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited ("Mkango") pursuant to certain Mkango supply rights to HyProMag USA.
Highlights 
The PFS evaluated two development options, both based on modular production systems: Case 1 - Recycled feedstock only: HPMS recycling of magnet scrap to produce NdFeB alloy powder, sintered magnet blocks, finished and packaged magnets; and 
Case 2 - Recycled and primary feedstock: as Case 1, with the additional capex to support primary NdFeB alloy as a feedstock to produce NdFeB alloy powder, sintered magnet blocks, finished and packaged magnets. 
Project economics with a post-tax NPV [iv] , [v] of US$1,854 million (Case 2) to US$2,062 million (Case 1) for the three new plants (excluding the Northlake Texas Facility), post-tax IRR of 31% (Case 2) to 36% (Case 1) and a Profitability Index (post-tax NPV divided by capital cost) of approximately 2.8x to 3.3x, based on forecast prices [vi] and a Class 3 AACE [vii] capital cost estimate of approximately US$656 million (Case 2) to US$623 million (Case 1), respectively, with a payback of 3 years (Case 2) and 2.3 years (Case 1). 
Competitive Manufacturing Costs. For the first PFS Plant in 2030, the PFS estimates an All-In Sustaining Cost ("AISC") of approximately US$41.6 per kg ( Case 2 ) to US$37.4 per kg ( Case 1 ) of finished NdFeB products sold. AISC includes all downstream processing and finishing costs, including plating and epoxy coating. Based on forecast market prices and the forecast product mix, the weighted average realized all-in selling price in 2030 is estimated at approximately US$100.5 per kg, supporting strong margins and attractive project returns.
Combined HyProMag USA platform value: The combined post-tax NPV range of the proposed Northlake Texas Facility and the potential PFS plants is estimated at US$2.6 billion to US$2.8 billion. 
The staged approach for the Northlake Texas Facility: [viii] Updated post-tax NPV of approximately US$723 [ix] , [x] , [xi] , [xii] million based on forecast prices and a capital cost estimate of approximately US$167 million [xiii] , increased due to the phased construction approach and the finalization of equipment orders. The reduction from the post-tax NPV of approximately US$797 million announced on June 22, 2026, reflects the later construction timetable, the higher capital costs and updated operating cost assumptions consistent with the PFS. 
Potential fourfold increase in U.S. magnet producing capacity: from approximately 1,048 metric tons per year of salable NdFeB magnets at the Northlake Texas Facility to approximately 4,192 metric tons per year across four plants by 2034. Phase 1 of the Northlake Texas Facility is expected to be commissioned in mid-2028. 
Integrated alloy processing and centralized finishing: The Central Texas Hub is expected to incorporate Vacuum Induction Melting ("VIM") and strip-casting operations, allowing the platform to process NdFeB alloy, provide magnet plating, passivation, coating, quality assurance and customer qualification for all plants. 
Higher-value magnet production: The production configuration would incorporate grain boundary diffusion ("GBD") capability, which would significantly increase the proportion of higher-value NdFeB magnet products. High-grade magnet production would increase from approximately 10% to 20% of total magnet output, supporting enhanced product mix, market access and project economics. 
Low-carbon production: supported by a previously completed carbon footprint of approximately 2.35 kg CO₂-eq per kilogram of NdFeB sintered block product for the Northlake Texas Facility[xiv] . 
Commercial qualification pathway: Product performance data and customer validation are underway with potential U.S. offtake customers, with the support of the HyProMag Group. 
Additional revenue opportunities: The platform would provide future opportunities for third-party magnet finishing activities, supporting enhanced utilization of manufacturing infrastructure and potential additional revenue streams. 
The platform is expected to play a key role in re-establishing domestic NdFeB magnet manufacturing: in the United States, creating approximately 300 jobs across Texas, South Carolina, and Nevada, in addition to the 100 positions at the Northlake Texas Facility.
Independent PFS: completed by PegasusTSI Inc. and BBA USA Inc. with support from HyProMag's international teams and the University of Birmingham, UK. Subject to ongoing review, the expansion strategy is expected to progress to a Feasibility Study at the appropriate time. 
Julian Treger, Chief Executive Officer of CoTec, commented : "This Pre-Feasibility Study confirms the opportunity to establish a significant domestic rare earth magnet manufacturing platform in the United States. The Study demonstrates robust economics and a pathway to producing higher-value NdFeB magnet products for strategically important sectors including advanced manufacturing, energy, defense and AI-driven technologies. Importantly, the platform is designed with the flexibility to utilize primary alloy feedstock alongside recycled materials, providing greater supply chain resilience and supporting long-term operational competitiveness. The results highlight the platform's potential to create substantial long-term value while strengthening the U.S. rare earth magnet supply chain." 
Professor Allan Walton, Founder of HyProMag and Head of the Magnetic Materials Group at the University of Birmingham, commented: "The objective of the HyProMag platform has always been to demonstrate that HPMS technology can recover rare earth magnetic materials and convert them into high-performance commercial magnet products. The PFS outlines a pathway to scaling that capability through an integrated manufacturing platform incorporating magnet production, finishing and product qualification. Importantly, the enhanced production configuration would support the manufacture of a broader range of commercial magnet products for demanding industrial applications, while the inclusion of finishing, quality assurance and product development capabilities provides a foundation for continued product optimization and customer qualification." 
Platform Configuration 
The PFS assessed three new production plants in South Carolina, Nevada and a second location in Texas, which would operate alongside the Northlake Texas Facility. Each plant is intended to process feedstock, operate HPMS and produce unfinished sintered NdFeB blocks.
The Central Texas Hub, located within the second Texas plant, is expected to incorporate alloy processing (VIM and strip-casting), GBD, machining, plating, passivation, epoxy coating, quality assurance, product qualification and technology development capabilities.
Under the proposed configuration, unfinished sintered blocks produced from South Carolina, Nevada and the second facility in Texas would be transferred to the Central Texas Hub for advanced manufacturing and finishing. The Central Texas Hub is also designed to support future partnerships with specialist manufacturing and finishing providers, enabling the efficient scaling of advanced magnet production capability.
Higher-Value Magnet Production 
A key outcome of the PFS was the optimization of the manufacturing configuration to increase production of higher-value NdFeB magnet products. This enhanced product mix would be supported by further incorporation of GBD technology, which enables the production of higher-performance magnet grades required for demanding applications across medical, industrial automation, robotics, energy infrastructure and advanced manufacturing markets.
The increased proportion of higher-value magnet products would broaden exposure to premium end-use applications and is expected to support improved revenues, stronger operating margins and enhanced overall project returns.
Recycling of Magnet End Cuts By-Products 
The PFS plants are designed to recover and reprocess manufacturing residues, including magnet machining end cuts, through the HPMS process, maximizing the use of rare earth materials. This integrated approach would support both production flexibility and the circular manufacturing characteristics of the HyProMag platform.
Integrated Manufacturing Platform 
The Central Texas Hub is expected to create operating synergies through shared infrastructure and integrated processing capabilities. The Study indicates that the combination of integrated alloy processing, magnet manufacturing, finishing operations and flexible feedstock sourcing has the potential to support a competitive cost position for domestically manufactured rare earth magnet products. HyProMag USA believes these advantages will support the supply of U.S. manufactured magnets at competitive prices while providing customers with the benefits of domestic supply-chain security, traceability and low-carbon production.
The Central Texas Hub is also expected to evolve into an advanced manufacturing, product qualification and technology development center serving the broader manufacturing platform. In addition to supporting HyProMag USA production, the facility would provide future opportunities to support third-party magnet finishing activities, creating the potential for additional revenue streams and improved utilization of manufacturing infrastructure.
The proposed technology and product development center would leverage expertise from the wider HyProMag Group and the University of Birmingham's Magnetic Materials Group, supporting development, qualification and optimization of commercial magnet products.
Flexible Feedstock Platform 
A key outcome of the independent PFS is the flexibility of a manufacturing platform capable of utilizing both recycled NdFeB materials and primary alloy feedstocks. This flexible sourcing model is expected to enhance supply-chain resilience, support production growth and provide the ability to optimize raw material inputs in response to market conditions and customer requirements. HPMS technology provides the foundation for processing recycled magnetic materials and integrating them into the broader manufacturing platform.
Advancing Commercial Magnet Qualification with HyProMag Group 
Commercial magnet qualification activities continue across the wider HyProMag Group in the United Kingdom and Germany. These activities are expected to support qualification of future U.S.-produced magnet products, accelerate customer onboarding and reduce commercialization risk as the U.S. manufacturing platform expands. HyProMag USA believes this provides a meaningful advantage by allowing future U.S. operations to build upon existing technical and commercial progress rather than initiating qualification programs from a standing start.
About HyProMag USA 
HyProMag USA is developing advanced rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing operations to establish a secure domestic U.S. supply chain for NdFeB magnets, essential components for AI infrastructure, defense systems, robotics, electric vehicles, and advanced electronics. Leveraging the revolutionary HPMS technology, developed over 15 years with over US$100 million in R&D investment, HyProMag USA is designed to deliver faster magnet-to-magnet short-loop recycling that uses 88% less energy and reduces carbon emissions by 85% compared to conventional methods. HPMS accepts a wide range of magnet-bearing feedstocks - including end-of-life EV motors, data-center and industrial equipment, consumer electronics, and manufacturing scrap - enabling recovery of magnet-grade material without chemical processing.
Ownership 
HyProMag USA LLC is owned 50:50 by CoTec and HyProMag Limited. HyProMag Limited is 100% owned by Maginito Limited, which is owned 79.4% by Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited (AIM/TSX-V: MKA) and 20.6% by CoTec.
For more information on HyProMag USA, please visit www.hypromagusa.com 
About CoTec 
CoTec Holdings Corp. ( TSXV:CTH )(OTCQX:CTHCF) is redefining the future of resource extraction and recycling. Focused on rare earth magnets and strategic materials, CoTec integrates breakthrough technologies with strategic assets to unlock secure, sustainable, and low-cost supply chains.
CoTec's mission is clear: accelerate the energy transition while strengthening strategic mineral supply chains for the countries we operate in. By investing in and deploying disruptive technologies, the Company delivers capital-efficient, scalable solutions that transform marginal assets, tailings, waste streams, and recycled products into high-value critical minerals.
From its HyProMag USA magnet recycling joint venture in Texas, to iron tailings reprocessing and reclamation in Québec, to next-generation copper and iron solutions backed by global majors, CoTec is building a diversified portfolio with long-term growth, rapid cash flow potential, and high barriers to entry. The result is a differentiated platform at the intersection of technology, sustainability, and strategic materials.
For more information, please visit www.cotec.ca

Regional production plans and new separator designs are sharpening competition around supply reliability, safety performance and customer qualification.
The global polypropylene battery separator market was valued at US$6.53 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach US$28.31 billion by 2035, growing at a CAGR of 15.8% from 2026 to 2035, according to DataM Intelligence. Lithium-ion batteries accounted for 72.5% of the market in 2025. Asia-Pacific held a 64.89% share, while North America is forecast to be the fastest-growing region. 
Battery separators must keep the electrodes apart while allowing ions to pass through the electrolyte. For polypropylene (PP) separators, competitive performance increasingly depends on film thickness, pore structure, mechanical strength, coating quality and consistency across production runs. Cell manufacturers qualify separators for particular chemistries and formats, so expanding capacity alone does not guarantee sales. Suppliers must meet customer specifications and demonstrate reliable output at scale.

Recent Developments
- Japan updated its battery industry strategy: In June 2026, METI cited structural oversupply and supply-chain risks, while highlighting energy-storage requirements associated with advanced power demand, including AI data centers. The strategy adds supply resilience and cost discipline to Japan's battery-industry priorities. 
- SEMCORP reported results for new separator designs: In June, the company said cells using its pure-polyolefin and polyolefin/ceramic-coated separators passed impact and hot-box tests and retained more than 91% capacity after 1,000 cycles in its evaluations. These are company-reported test results. 
- Asahi Kasei opened a coating line in North Carolina: The company held an August 20 ceremony for a new wet-process Hipore separator coating line at its existing Celgard facility, adding North American coating and supply capabilities. 
- SEMCORP began production at a Phase II line in Yuxi: On August 30, SEMCORP announced that the first production line of the project had been commissioned, starting a new capacity ramp-up phase. 
- ENTEK continued development of its Indiana separator plant: The company lists a Phase I capacity deployment of 700 million square metres and targets a Q4 2026 start of production. These remain company project targets, with commercial output dependent on construction, commissioning and qualification. 
- Sumitomo Chemical consolidated its PERVIO separator operations: The company's restructuring plan called for production at Ohe Works to cease and manufacturing functions to move to subsidiary SSLM by the end of March 2026. The change illustrates how established Japanese suppliers are adjusting their production footprints in a competitive market. 
United States & Japan Market Opportunities
United States: 
The clearest opportunity is to qualify local separator production and coating for battery manufacturers seeking closer supply and technical support. Asahi Kasei's North Carolina line adds coating capability at an established site, while ENTEK's Indiana project is aimed at wet-process separator manufacturing. Their different approaches show that the domestic opportunity spans new film production, coating, equipment, quality control and testing. The commercial test will be how quickly each line reaches reliable output and passes customer qualification. 
Japan: 
Japan's established battery-material companies can compete through separator engineering, coatings and close technical work with cell and automotive manufacturers. METI's revised battery strategy brings supply-chain risk and storage needs into the policy discussion. Meanwhile, Sumitomo Chemical's PERVIO reorganization reflects pressure to streamline production. Companies assessing Japanese opportunities should weigh customer access and local technical collaboration against the cost and utilization of maintaining multiple manufacturing sites. 
Market Segmentation
DataM Intelligence segments the market by thickness, layer, battery type, technology, end user and region. Thickness categories include below 20 μm, 20-50 μm, 50-100 μm and above 100 μm. Layer categories include single-layer, multilayer, microporous and other structures. Battery types include lithium-ion, lead-acid and others; technology includes dry and wet processes. End users span energy and power, electronics, automotive, telecommunications, aerospace and defense, medical and other markets. 
Segment Analysis: Lithium-Ion Batteries
Lithium-ion batteries accounted for 72.5% of the market in 2025, supported by separator use across EVs, energy storage and consumer electronics. This segment is not a uniform product market: cell makers set separator requirements around chemistry, electrode design, electrolyte, charging profile and form factor. That makes customer qualification and product consistency central to competition. 
The opportunity lies in supplying qualified separator grades that meet cell-specific performance targets. Automotive programs put particular weight on safety, durability and stable supply over long production cycles. Electronics customers may prioritize compact cell design and energy density, while stationary storage applications emphasize dependable operation over extended cycling. Suppliers that can adapt thickness, pore structure and coating to these requirements may win a broader range of programs, but each new grade can add testing and manufacturing complexity.
Battery chemistry changes can also shift requirements. A separator design suited to one cell architecture may not automatically transfer to another. Product development and capacity planning therefore depend on close collaboration with cell manufacturers-not simply forecasts of overall lithium-ion production.

Segment Analysis: Dry and Wet Technologies
The market includes dry-process and wet-process separators, but the two processes should not be treated as interchangeable. Dry processing is associated with PP separators and forms pores through stretching and related film-manufacturing steps. Its commercial appeal can include a simpler process route and cost-efficient production, with product value depending on pore uniformity, mechanical strength, film thickness and fit with the battery design.
Wet processing uses a different pore-forming route and is widely associated with PE separator products. ENTEK, for example, describes its lithium-ion separators as wet-process, biaxially oriented PE products, offered in coated and uncoated formats. It also identifies thickness, air permeability and porosity as characteristics that can be tailored with customers. This distinction matters when assessing the PP market: competitors may operate across the broader polyolefin separator sector without every product being made from polypropylene. 
Technology selection depends on the target cell's performance needs and manufacturing economics. Cell makers evaluate separator properties, coating compatibility, yield, operating cost and production-line fit. Suppliers, in turn, need to demonstrate repeatable quality and adequate scale. New plants and coating lines may widen the regional supply base, but their commercial value depends on qualified output-not announced nameplate capacity alone.
Company Profiles
- Asahi Kasei Corporation - Asahi Kasei supplies wet-process Hipore and dry-process Celgard lithium-ion separators. Celgard offers single- and multilayer configurations, different film thicknesses and widths, and optional functional coatings. The company's North Carolina coating line adds local processing for Hipore products at an existing Celgard site, giving it a combined product and manufacturing footprint in North America. 
- ENTEK International - ENTEK manufactures wet-process, biaxially oriented PE separators for lithium-ion batteries, with coated and uncoated options. Its product specifications can be customized around thickness, air permeability and porosity. The company is building a large Indiana facility, with a stated Phase I capacity deployment of 700 million m2 and a Q4 2026 production target. Its U.S. expansion will depend on commissioning and customer qualification. 
- SEMCORP - SEMCORP's lithium-ion separator business combines product development with large-scale manufacturing. Its recent updates include evaluations of pure-polyolefin and ceramic-coated designs, as well as the commissioning of a Phase II production line at Yuxi. Together, these developments highlight its focus on functional coatings, battery performance and capacity expansion. 
- Toray Industries - Toray's film portfolio includes SETELA battery separator film for lithium-ion batteries and TORAYFAN polypropylene film. The company identifies SETELA as a microporous film used in batteries for mobile devices and EVs. Its separator R&D includes product functionality, quality improvement, manufacturing-process development and cost reduction. 
- Sumitomo Chemical - Sumitomo Chemical markets PERVIO lithium-ion battery separators. It announced a reorganization of the business that consolidated manufacturing and related functions at subsidiary SSLM, with production at Ohe Works scheduled to end by March 2026. The restructuring reflects the need to align production sites and operating costs with customer demand and competitive conditions.

24 October 2026 - 10:51

According to the Swedish Defence Materiel Administration (FMV) , new fire-control instruments supplied by Safran Electronics & Defense are being handed over to the Swedish Armed Forces. The programme covers 260 instruments, with an initial handover of 205 equipment cases and further deliveries planned through 2028. 
FMV announced on October 23 that the new systems are designed to improve the Swedish Armed Forces’ ability to observe, identify and locate targets, as well as coordinate indirect fire.
The main component is an electro-optical binocular system equipped with an infrared camera, laser rangefinder, compass and Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) module.
According to FMV, the system also includes digital mapping software, image fusion and other support functions. Data collected by the equipment can be transmitted to firing units and other military systems through command-and-control and communications interfaces.
For fire-control teams requiring greater precision, FMV is also providing a north-seeking gyroscope on which the instrument can be mounted. The agency said the equipment uses the Earth’s rotation to determine bearings with high accuracy.
FMV added that the new instrument is approximately 10 kilograms lighter than its predecessor, making it easier for personnel to carry and operate.
Further deliveries planned through 2028
The programme covers 260 fire-control instruments, along with testing and repair equipment and spare parts intended to support maintenance by the Swedish Armed Forces.
According to FMV, the first stage involves handing over 205 cases containing instruments and associated spare parts, with further deliveries continuing through 2028.
The agency signed a contract worth approximately SEK 488 million with Safran Electronics & Defense in September 2025. The system, commercially known as MOTI SHARPCROW, is intended for fire-control teams in the Swedish Army, Navy and Home Guard.
FMV said the new equipment will support the planning, execution and assessment of indirect-fire missions.

Moderna and Merck’s personalized mRNA cancer vaccine cuts melanoma relapse risk by 42%
SoYeon Kim
2026.10.23 11:43 KST
Share
Font -
Font +
Print
Moderna and Merck unveil first Phase 3 results
A cancer vaccine developed by Moderna and Merck has been shown to markedly reduce the likelihood of cancer recurrence in melanoma patients. Image: Fletcher, via Wikimedia Commons
A personalized “messenger RNA (mRNA) cancer vaccine,” tailored to each patient’s individual tumor, has reduced the risk of recurrence or death in melanoma patients by up to 42% in a Phase 3 clinical trial. Cancer vaccines are used to help treat cancers that have already developed or to prevent recurrence and metastasis after surgery.
 
Pharmaceutical companies Moderna and Merck announced on the 22nd (local time) that their mRNA-based cancer vaccine Intismeran significantly lowered the risk of cancer recurrence in melanoma patients. This is the first time an mRNA-based cancer vaccine has delivered positive results in a Phase 3 trial.
 
Moderna and Merck had already reported in August that the clinical trial of Intismeran was successful, but the detailed findings were scheduled to be presented on the 24th (local time) at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO). According to international outlets including AP and Reuters, some data were leaked on the afternoon of the 22nd, prompting Moderna and Merck to move up their timetable and release the full results that same day.
 
mRNA cancer vaccines are medicines that train a patient’s immune cells to recognize and attack cancer cells. Cells are collected from the patient’s tumor to identify genetic mutations unique to cancer cells that are absent in normal cells. The proteins generated by these mutations are called “neoantigens.”
 
Researchers select the neoantigens most likely to elicit a strong immune response and encode the genetic information for these neoantigens into mRNA. Once this mRNA is injected into the body, cells use the genetic information it carries to produce the neoantigens.
 
The body’s immune cells then recognize these neoantigens as targets and seek out and precisely destroy cancer cells that display the same neoantigens.
 
The joint research team from Moderna and Merck administered Merck’s immune checkpoint inhibitor Keytruda (pembrolizumab) to 1,137 high-risk melanoma patients whose tumors had been surgically removed. Two out of every three patients, selected at random, additionally received Intismeran, while the remaining patients received a placebo.
 
Melanoma is a type of skin cancer that arises from melanocytes, the pigment-producing cells that make melanin. After two years, 82% of patients in the Intismeran group were alive without cancer recurrence, compared with 70% in the control group. The combination regimen of Intismeran plus Keytruda reduced the risk of cancer recurrence or death by 42% compared with Keytruda monotherapy.
 
Georgina Long, professor of melanoma medical oncology and translational research at the University of Sydney in Australia, who led the study, said, “This approach enhances antitumor immune responses by designing treatment to match the unique mutational profile of a patient’s tumor,” adding, “As clinical research continues in other tumor types and various treatment settings, these findings will provide valuable insights into Intismeran and how best to use it.”
 
Moderna and Merck are conducting a broad clinical program called INTerpath to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Intismeran both in combination with other anticancer therapies such as Keytruda and as a monotherapy.
 
The current INTerpath program includes nine Phase 2 and Phase 3 trials involving patients with a range of different cancers.
 
AP reported that independent experts not involved in the study also regard these Phase 3 results as a groundbreaking advance in the field of cancer vaccines. Michael Atkins, deputy director of the Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center at Georgetown University in the United States, said, “mRNA cancer vaccines represent a major step forward for science and oncology because they can be applied to a wide variety of cancers.”

content_text:
[News] Infineon and NVIDIA Expand GaN Power Collaboration for AI Data Centers
2026-10-23 
Emerging Technologies 
editor 
On October 21, Infineon Technologies announced an expanded collaboration with NVIDIA in AI data center power delivery during NVIDIA’s GTC developer conference in Berlin. The two companies will jointly develop high-voltage intermediate bus converter (IBC) solutions based on gallium nitride (GaN) power devices for 800V direct current (800V DC) architectures.
The expanded collaboration builds on the companies’ 800V DC power delivery initiative launched in 2025. It focuses on power conversion for high-power AI racks and will also support hot-swappable server rack maintenance.
The high-voltage IBC is a key component in the AI data center power delivery chain. Leveraging its CoolGaN product portfolio, Infineon will address multiple conversion configurations, including 800V-to-50V and 800V-to-12V, using high-frequency switching technology. The solutions are intended for NVIDIA’s MGX open modular reference architecture for AI factories.
The power architecture is designed for AI computing systems with power consumption of up to 1 MW per rack, with deployment expected to begin gradually in 2027.
Infineon and NVIDIA first announced their collaboration on 800V DC data center power delivery in May 2025. The initial initiative covered both silicon carbide (SiC) and GaN technologies.
The latest expansion places greater emphasis on GaN for intermediate bus conversion. The solutions aim to increase power density, reduce power losses across the delivery chain, and lower cooling hardware requirements. They are also designed to enable controlled pre-charging and discharging of server motherboards, as well as hot-swapping while the rack remains operational, helping reduce the risk of service disruptions during data center maintenance.
Beyond GaN-based IBCs, Infineon is supplying SiC devices, power protection components, and other power products for NVIDIA’s 800V DC ecosystem, covering the power delivery chain from the grid to AI processors.
NVIDIA’s 800V DC architecture is intended to simplify the multiple AC-to-DC and DC-to-DC conversion stages used in conventional data centers, reducing the number of conversion stages and associated components.
The ecosystem brings together power semiconductor suppliers, power system manufacturers, and data center infrastructure providers. Infineon is among the suppliers participating in the ecosystem with portfolios spanning SiC, GaN, and silicon-based power devices.

Park Kwang-sun, president of Applied Materials Korea, poses for a commemorative photo at the 19th Semiconductor Day ceremony held at the Grand InterContinental Seoul Parnas in Gangnam, Seoul, on Oct. 21. (Photo: Applied Materials Korea) 
Applied Materials Korea received an Industrial Service Medal in recognition of its contributions to strengthening South Korea's semiconductor industry competitiveness.
Park Kwang-sun, president of Applied Materials Korea, received the medal at the 19th Semiconductor Day ceremony held at the Grand InterContinental Seoul Parnas in Gangnam, Seoul, on Oct. 21.
Applied Materials Korea said the award recognized its efforts to expand the global technology innovation ecosystem and strengthen collaboration on next-generation semiconductor research and development (R&D). Park has promoted cooperation among domestic customers and suppliers and led efforts to build industry networks.
Applied Materials Korea is establishing the Applied Collaboration Center Korea in Osan, Gyeonggi Province, as a regional hub. The center will expand collaboration with major domestic customers and suppliers, supporting activities from early-stage R&D to mass-production validation. It aims to develop local talent and strengthen the competitiveness of South Korea's semiconductor ecosystem.
The company also invests in domestic startups. Applied Materials Korea works with approximately 100 local suppliers. It has established a $50 million fund with Korea Venture Investment Corp. (KVIC) to support promising domestic startups. The company also organizes technology symposiums and site visit programs for university students and provides semiconductor simulation software to university research laboratories.
Semiconductor Day was established by the Korea Semiconductor Industry Association in 2008. Each year, the association recognizes individuals who have contributed to strengthening the competitiveness of South Korea's semiconductor industry.

Investing.com -- British measurement firm Renishaw said on Thursday first-quarter revenue jumped 47% to a record £251.8 million, driven by demand from semiconductor and aerospace customers, but stopped short of raising its full-year guidance. 
Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list » 
The figure for the three months to Sept 30 was 47% higher than a weak comparator a year earlier and 3% above the fourth quarter of the last financial year, the company said in an unaudited trading update. 
At constant exchange rates, which strip out currency moves, revenue rose 48% from the previous year. 
Renishaw said it continues to expect "strong progress on revenue and operating margin for FY2027 as a whole." Revenue grew in all three business segments and all three regions. 
Position Measurement revenue rose 84% to a record £96.0 million from £52.1 million a year earlier, driven by demand for open optical and laser encoders used in semiconductor manufacturing equipment. 
Revenue was 17% above the fourth quarter. The order book grew further in the quarter, and Renishaw is investing in more production capacity for those products. It also saw rising demand for encoders for harsh environments in automation, robotics and space applications. 
Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks » 
Industrial Metrology revenue rose 28% to £130.8 million from £102 million a year earlier, and was 9% above the fourth quarter, on demand for five-axis coordinate measuring machines and shop-floor gauging systems, with a growing order book. 
Sales of sensors to machine tool and measuring machine makers also improved after a flat FY2026, with stronger sales into aerospace and defence, energy and consumer electronics. 
Specialised Technologies revenue rose 50% to £25 million from £16.7 million, led by additive manufacturing systems sold to aerospace and defence and medical customers. 
Revenue was below the £42.7 million of the fourth quarter, as expected, after what the company called an "exceptionally strong" period. 
The order book has strengthened. Spectroscopy revenue was marginally lower than a year earlier, though its order book also strengthened. Renishaw said the sale of its neurological business continues. 
Demand from semiconductor, aerospace and defence customers remains strong, and is now complemented by wider automation investment in other industries, the company said. 
Story Continues 
It is working to expand its supply chain and production capacity while remaining "mindful of the cyclical nature of demand over the medium term."

title: Sumitomo Chemical deepens India semiconductor push with Tata Electronics pact - Indiatimes

Sumitomo Chemical deepens India semiconductor push with Tata Electronics pact 
Sumitomo Chemical has signed an MoU with Tata Electronics to explore collaboration in semiconductor fabrication and materials supply, including a possible chemicals facility in India. The move reflects growing interest from upstream suppliers in India’s chip ambitions, where reliable access to high-purity chemicals and photoresists could shape future manufacturing capacity. 
ETChemicals 
Published On Oct 21, 2026 at 12:04 PM IST
Read by 2812 Professionals
Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook 
Bookmark 
India’s semiconductor ambitions are increasingly drawing in global materials suppliers, not just chip designers and fabricators. In a move that underlines that shift, Sumitomo Chemical has signed a memorandum of understanding with Tata Electronics to examine a possible collaboration in semiconductor fabrication and the supporting supply chain , according to specchemonline.com . 
The agreement is significant because semiconductor manufacturing depends on a tightly controlled ecosystem of chemicals, photoresists and high-purity inputs. Any serious effort to localise chip production in India will need those upstream materials to be available reliably, at scale and with consistent quality. That is the business opportunity Sumitomo Chemical appears to be targeting through the Tata partnership. 
What the agreement is meant to cover 
The companies plan to study specific steps that could help create a stable materials supply system for semiconductor manufacturing. One possibility being explored is the establishment of a semiconductor chemicals facility in India, which would give the Japanese supplier a local foothold in a market that is still building out its chip ecosystem. 
The MoU does not amount to a final investment decision, but it signals intent. For Tata Electronics , which is building its semiconductor ambitions in India, a dependable materials partner could be as important as equipment, talent and policy support. For Sumitomo Chemical, the arrangement offers a way to align with a customer base that may grow as India pushes harder into advanced electronics manufacturing. 
Why materials matter more than ever 
Semiconductor fabrication is often discussed through the lens of fabs, foundries and government incentives, but the industry is equally dependent on specialist materials. Photoresists and high-purity chemicals are essential in the patterning and processing steps that allow chips to be manufactured at advanced nodes. Supply disruptions in these inputs can quickly ripple through production schedules and yield outcomes. 
That is why localisation efforts are increasingly extending beyond assembly and packaging. Countries seeking to build semiconductor resilience are now looking at the full stack, including the chemicals that enable chipmaking in the first place. A domestic or regional supply base can reduce logistics risk, shorten lead times and improve control over quality assurance. 
Sumitomo Chemical is betting on semiconductor growth 
The semiconductor materials business has been positioned as a priority inside Sumitomo Chemical’s ICT and Mobility Solutions segment, which the Japanese group views as one of its growth engines. The company has built a reputation in advanced photoresists and semiconductor chemicals, particularly high-purity products used in demanding fabrication environments. 
Over the past few years, the company has expanded semiconductor chemicals capacity in Japan and South Korea while also setting up a new base in Texas. Earlier this year, it acquired Asia Union Electronic Chemical , which operates facilities in Taiwan and Nevada. The company has also started work at advanced high-purity chemical centres in Japan and South Korea, where it is developing new processes and recycling technologies. 
That sequence of investments suggests a broader strategy: deepen presence in major semiconductor geographies while improving supply resilience and technical capabilities. The India move fits that pattern, especially as chip manufacturing becomes more geographically diversified in response to geopolitical and supply chain concerns. 
India’s chip ecosystem is attracting upstream players 
India has spent the past few years trying to move from policy ambition to industrial execution in semiconductors . The country’s appeal is no longer limited to final-stage electronics assembly. Global suppliers are beginning to evaluate whether India can support the specialised materials and process infrastructure needed for chip fabrication. 
That shift matters because semiconductor projects are rarely built in isolation. A viable ecosystem requires chemical suppliers, gas suppliers, wafer handling, cleanroom services, logistics providers and a skilled technical workforce. The presence of a company such as Sumitomo Chemical would be a signal that India is moving closer to that broader industrial base. 
For Tata Electronics, the partnership could help strengthen its supply chain planning at a time when semiconductor manufacturing is becoming a strategic priority for large industrial groups in India. For Sumitomo Chemical, the arrangement could open a pathway into a market that combines scale potential with policy support for electronics manufacturing. 
Regional competition is also intensifying 
The India discussion comes as Japanese chemical companies continue to expand in other Asian semiconductor hubs. Another Japanese player, Nissan Chemical , has separately set up a wholly owned subsidiary in Zhangjiagang in Jiangsu province, China. That unit will manufacture anti-reflective coatings used in photoresists and multilayer semiconductor materials. 
Nissan Chemical has said demand for semiconductors in China has continued to rise, helped by digitalisation and other structural factors, while customers are also seeking more resilient supply chains. The parallel expansion by Japanese suppliers in China and India highlights a broader industry trend: materials companies are following chip manufacturing demand wherever it is likely to concentrate next. 
For India, the challenge will be to convert interest into durable industrial capacity. A materials facility, if it goes ahead, would not by itself create a complete semiconductor supply chain. But it would be an important marker of confidence, showing that upstream global suppliers are willing to commit capital and know-how to the country’s chip ambitions. 
The Tata Electronics tie-up therefore sits at the intersection of manufacturing policy, supply chain resilience and long-term industrial strategy. If the exploratory talks lead to a concrete project, it could become one of the more telling examples of how India’s semiconductor push is beginning to draw in the chemicals businesses that underpin the sector’s real economics.

ABB Robotics Brings Physical AI to Fashion Logistics 
2026-10-22 
From
Sariana Kunze
2 min Reading Time 
Related Vendors 
FAULHABER Drive Systems 
SIMTOS (Seoul International Machine Tool Show) 
ABB Robotics has launched its first fully integrated, camera-based Physical AI solution for logistics applications in the fashion industry.
ABB Robotics is launching its first end-to-end physical-AI solution for industrial applications: the Fashion Inductor and AI Robot Trainer. (Image: ABB Robotics) 
By integrating the AI Robot Trainer into the Fashion Inductor feature package, ABB Robotics aims to help system integrators implement, scale, and continuously optimize AI-powered applications for fashion logistics with less effort and risk.
“Physical AI is fundamentally changing what robots can do in industrial applications,” emphasizes Craig McDonnell, head of the Industries business line at ABB Robotics. “Some of the greatest potential of Physical AI lies in applications that, due to their high variability, have been difficult to automate until now.”
Designed to Meet the Demands of Fashion Logistics
The Fashion Inductor was developed specifically to meet the demands and accommodate the wide variety of the fashion and apparel logistics sector, where products, packaging, and operating conditions are constantly changing. Even today, the system is designed to enable high-performance sorting and separation under real-world logistics conditions—with a throughput of up to 1,300 items per hour per cell and a grasping accuracy of more than 99.5 percent. This is made possible by ABB Robotics’ AI-powered automatic path planning, the robots’ high motion precision, and the image processing technology developed specifically for this application.
Physical AI Features Reduce Effort by 75 Percent
The AI Robot Trainer adds camera-based Physical AI features designed to reduce development and commissioning efforts by up to 75 percent. The solution includes pre-trained AI models for image processing—specifically tailored to applications in fashion and apparel logistics—as well as application-specific tools and features for quickly retraining the models. This is intended to enable system integrators to implement applications without specialized AI expertise, adapt them to changing requirements, and continuously optimize them.
AI Robot Trainer Enables a Closed-Loop Workflow
The AI models are not only developed but also continuously optimized throughout the robot system’s entire lifecycle and adapted to real-world performance requirements and changing operating conditions. The AI Robot Trainer enables fast and structured retraining tailored to the specific robot cell within a so-called closed-loop workflow. In this process, the system monitors the robot’s performance, detects deviations, generates new training data for the models, and feeds improvements directly back to the robot.

Merck opens Korean chip materials plant to meet advanced memory demand
Published : Oct. 22, 2026 - 10:27:43
Add The Korea Herald on Google
Link copied!
Moon Joon-hyun 
Tech Reporter
Covers Korean companies at the center of global chips, AI and consumer technology, from Samsung and SK hynix to Apple suppliers
Subscribe + 
Merck Electronics CEO sees Korea as key market as company braces for potential doubling of chip materials demand
Benjamin Hein, CEO of Merck's Electronics business, speaks during a press conference in Seoul on Wednesday. (Merck Korea) 
German science and technology company Merck opened a new semiconductor materials plant in South Korea on Thursday, expanding local production of molybdenum as chipmakers adopt the metal for increasingly advanced memory chips.
The facility in Eumseong, North Chungcheong Province, will produce molybdenum dioxide dichloride, a chemical used to deposit ultrathin metal films during chip manufacturing. It will supply customers in Korea and elsewhere in Asia.
Benjamin Hein, CEO of Merck's Electronics business, described Korea as among the top three markets for semiconductor materials during a press conference in Seoul on Wednesday.
"What if the demand for semiconductor materials and solutions doubles within the next five years? Are we ready? We want to be ready," Hein said.
The plant will initially focus on materials for advanced 3D NAND flash memory, which increases storage capacity by stacking memory cells vertically.
Merck's Eumseong plant in North Chungcheong Province, where the German company opened a new molybdenum production facility for advanced semiconductor manufacturing on Thursday (Merck Korea) 
Samsung Electronics began using molybdenum in its ninth-generation V-NAND in 2024, while SK hynix has reportedly been preparing to introduce the metal in its next-generation 375-layer NAND.
Molybdenum offers an alternative to tungsten, whose electrical resistance becomes increasingly problematic as chipmakers shrink components and stack more layers. It can also reduce the need for barrier films that occupy valuable space inside microscopic structures.
Bing Han, executive vice president and head of Merck's Thin Films business, said adoption was beginning with NAND, with DRAM and logic chips expected to follow. "Eventually more of the smaller features will all move to Moly," Han said, while acknowledging that the pace of adoption depends on individual customers.
Merck will combine precursor production in Eumseong with chemical delivery systems manufactured at its Ansan facility in Gyeonggi Province. The company says the integrated system can use more than 99 percent of the material loaded into its containers, potentially reducing waste and manufacturing costs.
"Local for local is everything," Han said. "You can have the best offering, but you have to have your best offering in the right location."
The expansion forms part of Merck's 600 million euro ($674 million) investment program announced in 2021. Merck disclosed plans for the molybdenum facility in February, but declined to reveal its investment cost or production capacity.
Hein also identified advanced packaging, which combines multiple chips into increasingly complex systems, as another growth area. He said manufacturers face an immediate shortage of packaging capacity, with further technological changes expected over the next three to five years.
"On advanced packaging, short term, there is simply not enough capacity," he said. "So on the immediate, it is about debottlenecking."

Sales totaled $6.6 billion for the quarter. Core revenue growth excluding respiratory testing revenue was 5.5%, accelerating 100 basis points from the second quarter. Respiratory revenue created an approximately 250-basis-point headwind, resulting in reported core revenue growth of 3%.

Adjusted operating profit margin rose 110 basis points to 29%, aided primarily by operational execution and a modest benefit from tariff refunds received during the quarter. Adjusted diluted earnings per share increased about 11.5% to $2.11. The company generated $1.6 billion of free cash flow in the quarter and $4 billion through the first nine months of the year. 
New CEO Outlines Growth Priorities 
President and Chief Executive Officer Julie Sawyer Montgomery, in her first earnings call as CEO, said the company’s objective is to become the “defining leader in Life Sciences and Diagnostics” by gaining share more consistently, delivering profitable growth and helping customers improve patient outcomes. 
3 Stocks Offering Strong Value and Stability 
Montgomery said Danaher’s focus is shifting from portfolio reshaping toward generating more growth from its existing businesses. She outlined four strategic priorities: commercial excellence, innovation, talent and disciplined capital allocation. 
The company’s most immediate opportunity is commercial execution, according to Montgomery. She said Danaher intends to preserve the customer intimacy and accountability of its operating-company structure while making it easier for customers to access capabilities across the broader organization. 
In Diagnostics, she said coordinated engagement by leaders from different businesses with major customers has created “several hundred millions of dollars of opportunity” in a short period. Montgomery said Danaher views higher core growth, profitable core growth and “unambiguous share gain” as the measures of progress. 
Montgomery also emphasized artificial intelligence as an opportunity both internally and for customers. Danaher recently announced an AI-powered autonomous laboratory at Abcam that combines AI, robotics and technologies from Cytiva, Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, Genedata, IDT and Molecular Devices. The company said the connected design, make and test workflow is designed to help researchers move from an idea to a validated reagent up to eight times faster and produce up to 10 times higher volume than existing models.

Montgomery said the company is also working with Anthropic on standards intended to make instruments easier to connect with other agents and instruments.

Biotechnology core revenue increased 5% in the third quarter. Bioprocessing revenue grew toward the upper end of the mid-single-digit range, exceeding the company’s expectations. Consumables increased mid-single digits, led by upstream consumables, while equipment revenue grew low single digits. Bioprocessing orders increased in the mid-teens, led by upstream consumables and reagents. 
Chief Financial Officer Matt Gugino said Danaher maintained its expectation for mid-single-digit bioprocessing core revenue growth for the full year. He said the company continues to view bioprocessing as a long-term high-single-digit growth business, supported by commercial production activity and a pipeline of new programs. 
Life Sciences core revenue rose 4.5%. Pall’s applied filtration business grew mid-single digits, driven by aerospace and microelectronics demand. Life Sciences instruments also increased mid-single digits, with SCIEX benefiting from pharma and biopharma demand, improving U.S. academic spending and momentum for products including the ZenoTOF 8600. 
Beckman Coulter Life Sciences reported strong performance, including increased demand for AI-enabled automation solutions and services. Collectively, Life Sciences consumables businesses grew low single digits, with IDT benefiting from molecular residual disease and next-generation sequencing products, while Abcam experienced improving academic demand and traction with pharma and biopharma customers. 
Diagnostics core revenue excluding respiratory testing increased 7%. Respiratory revenue represented an approximately 650-basis-point headwind, leaving total segment core growth of 50 basis points. Clinical Diagnostics businesses grew mid-single digits, led by Leica Biosystems’ momentum in digital pathology and advanced staining. Beckman Coulter Diagnostics delivered its highest core-growth quarter in more than two years, according to the company. 
Cepheid’s non-respiratory molecular diagnostics business grew low double digits, driven by group A strep, virology and sexual-health assays. Respiratory revenue was approximately $350 million, declining year over year due mainly to lower global infection rates, though it was modestly above the company’s expectations as customers purchased ahead of the respiratory season. 
Outlook and Capital Deployment 
For the fourth quarter, Danaher expects core revenue growth excluding respiratory revenue of 4% to 5%. Respiratory revenue is expected to be an approximately 150-basis-point headwind, while adjusted operating profit margin is projected at about 29.5%. 
The company increased its full-year 2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance to $8.57 to $8.62, from a prior range of $8.45 to $8.60. Gugino said the new range reflects third-quarter outperformance and represents double-digit year-over-year EPS growth. 
For 2027, Danaher said it views 4% to 5% core revenue growth excluding respiratory revenue as the appropriate starting point based on current market conditions, though formal guidance will be provided in January. The company is using $1.5 billion in respiratory revenue as its planning assumption for both 2026 and as a starting point for 2027, while noting that seasonal flu variability can affect that figure. 
On acquisitions, Montgomery said M&A remains Danaher’s preferred capital-allocation approach and that the company will continue to seek strategically compounding transactions under its established investment criteria. Masimo delivered high-single-digit revenue growth in its first full quarter as part of Danaher, according to Montgomery. She said integration is progressing with cost-savings and commercial-synergy opportunities, while Masimo recently received FDA clearance for its smartSET platform to help detect atrial fibrillation. 
Danaher also said reshoring activity in bioprocessing is currently centered on brownfield projects, while larger greenfield projects remain largely in planning stages. Montgomery said the company sees the opportunity as potentially reaching $1 billion in the U.S., with the more significant revenue impact expected to begin in 2028 and develop over several years.

content_text:
Corning to invest $585M, add 414 jobs in Wilmington expansion 
Corning Inc. will invest $585 million at its Wilmington campus and add 414 jobs over the next five years, expanding one of the world’s largest optical fiber man 
By Hannah Hall 
Published : Oct. 21, 2026 at 10:31 AM EDT 
Share 
Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google 
WILMINGTON, N.C. (WECT) - Corning Inc. will invest $585 million at its Wilmington campus and add 414 jobs over the next five years, expanding one of the world’s largest optical fiber manufacturing plants.
The New York-based company announced the expansion Wednesday after the Wilmington City Council and New Hanover County Commissioners approved a package of incentives earlier this week to expand its operations. 
“We’re proud to expand our presence in Wilmington, where Corning made history with the world’s first optical fiber manufacturing plant and where our people continue to make the fiber that is critical to next-generation networks,” said John McGirr, senior vice president and general manager of Corning Optical Fiber and Cable.
NHC Commissioners approve incentive for Corning Inc. to expand in Wilmington 
Wilmington council backs $2 million deal to sweeten odds of landing Corning expansion 
Wilmington competed with several other locations for the project, known as “Project Pearl 2.” The project will supply fiber for next-generation networks and support long-term customer agreements, according to Corning.
The new jobs are expected to pay an average salary of more than $85,000 a year, and the company said the expansion will add more than $35 million in annual payroll for the region.
“Corning has been part of New Hanover County for decades, and when a company with that track record is ready to grow, this Board wants that growth to happen here,” said LeAnn Pierce, Chair of the New Hanover County Board of Commissioners. “Those are good paychecks for families in our community. The grant is tied to those jobs and that investment, and that is exactly how it should work.”
The company has maintained a civic commitment to the Wilmington area for 60 years, partnering with Cape Fear Community College on the Corning Technician Pipeline Program and investing in STEM education in local schools.
“It’s impossible to overstate how important this company is to Greater Wilmington,” said Scott Satterfield, CEO of Wilmington Business Development.

content_text:
Toray develops polyester-nylon fiber with recycled content
The company says both the polyester and nylon components of its new fiber incorporate recycled materials.
Photo courtesy of Toray 
Posted by
Chris Voloschuk, Associate Editor 
Published October 21, 2026
Listen to article 
/ 
Toray Industries Inc. recently announced it had developed a polyester-nylon fiber containing at least 93 percent recycled content by mass, based on the total weight of the raw yarn.
The Japan-based company says the percentage applies to the newly developed raw yarn and does not represent the recycled content of the finished fabric or garment. It says the breakthrough drew on technologies the company cultivated through its &+ (and plus) recycled fiber brand, adding that the polyester and nylon components of the fiber incorporate recycled materials.
Composite fibers can provide added functionality, sophisticated textures and subtle visual effects, Toray says, but combining different polymers makes it difficult to use high proportions of recycled materials while maintaining consistent quality. The company says it tapped into its expertise in polymer design and composite spinning to overcome the challenge and achieve a product containing at least 93 percent recycled content by mass, and it plans to verify the technology’s viability for mass production and continue research to increase recycled content in composite fibers.
“The fashion industry is showing increasing interest in material containing recycled content,” Toray says. “Materials for high-end and luxury applications must also deliver exceptional aesthetic qualities, including appearance, tailoring and drape, texture and durability.”
These considerations prompted Toray to create Artirosa CX, which it says incorporates the newly developed fiber. The company notes that the recycled content in each Artirosa CX fabric may vary depending on its composition.
The company says Artirosa CX features a “dense, finely textured surface and a crisp, sophisticated feel,” adding that fabric design and finishing also can impart practical properties like waterproofing, durable water repellency and wind resistance. 
“Rather than emphasizing the distinctive appearance typical of conventional functional materials, Artirosa CX refines that look into an elegant, sophisticated texture,” Toray says. “The result is a cleaner, more contemporary urban aesthetic.”
Toray says it intends to market Artirosa CX for wide-ranging applications, including men’s and women’s outerwear, urban outdoor wear and premium casual wear. The company expects to launch the product in late-2027 and is targeting initial year sales of 200,000 meters (around 218,722 yards) of material.

Thermo Fisher posts higher third-quarter revenue and earnings as margins improve Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc ( NYSE:TMO , XETRA:TN8 ) increased third-quarter revenue by 9% to $12.14 billion, while adjusted earnings per share rose 15% to $6.68. 
Revenue for the three months ended September 2026 increased from $11.12 billion a year earlier, with organic revenue growth, which excludes the effects of acquisitions, disposals and currency movements, reaching 6%. 
Adjusted operating income rose 15% to $2.97 billion, while adjusted operating margin increased to 24.5% from 23.3% in the same period last year. 
The company's generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) diluted earnings per share increased 9% to $4.64, while GAAP operating income rose 17% to $2.26 billion. 
GAAP operating margin improved to 18.6% from 17.4%, indicating that the company retained a larger share of revenue as operating profit. 
Thermo Fisher chief executive Marc Casper said the company's growth strategy and its Practical Process Improvement (PPI) Business System supported its performance during the quarter. 
The company launched several products during the period, including a mass spectrometer designed for isotope ratio analysis, an electron detector for advanced materials research and a new autoimmune screening test cleared by the US Food and Drug Administration. 
Thermo Fisher also partnered with Mayo Clinic to launch Precure, an initiative combining data from more than one million patient samples with its proteomics technologies to support disease research, earlier detection and precision medicine. 
In South Korea, the company opened its first artificial intelligence and automation innovation centre to help customers improve research and development productivity. 
Thermo Fisher also opened a highly automated distribution centre in Kentucky to improve supply chain speed and flexibility across North America. 
The company completed the previously announced sale of its microbiology business during the quarter as part of its capital deployment strategy. 
Thermo Fisher said it would provide updated financial guidance for 2026 during its third-quarter earnings conference call. 
Shares were down around 2% in early Wednesday morning trading.

New $1.3 billion agreement supports further expansion in South Korea, building on the companies' recent Arizona collaboration 
TEMPE, Ariz., October 21, 2026 --( BUSINESS WIRE )--Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR), a leading provider of outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services, today announced additional investments in South Korea for capacity expansion initiatives with NVIDIA. With this latest commitment, Amkor's multi-year agreements with NVIDIA in Arizona and South Korea total $3 billion. The initiatives support growing demand for next-generation AI and accelerated computing platforms. 
Advanced packaging technologies are essential to enabling the performance, power efficiency and integration required for next-generation computing systems. The prepayments align Amkor's manufacturing capacity with NVIDIA's long-term growth plans and support increasing demand for advanced packaging solutions. 
"Our partnership with NVIDIA underscores the critical role advanced packaging plays in enabling next-generation AI platforms," said Kevin Engel, president and chief executive officer of Amkor Technology. "These investments build on our global manufacturing footprint and strengthen our ability to support customers through our operations in both the United States and South Korea." 
"Growing demand for accelerated computing is increasing the need for advanced packaging capacity," said Debora Shoquist, executive vice president, operations of NVIDIA. "Our work with Amkor helps us scale production of current and next-generation platforms while strengthening the resilience of our global supply chain." 
This collaboration further strengthens Amkor's role as a strategic manufacturing partner for NVIDIA and reinforces the companies' shared commitment to supporting the continued expansion of AI infrastructure. 
Amkor will also exhibit at NVIDIA GTC Washington, D.C. from Nov. 30 - Dec. 3, where the company will showcase its advanced packaging and test capabilities and engage with customers, policymakers and industry leaders. 
About Amkor Technology, Inc. 
Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR) is the world's largest U.S. headquartered OSAT and is a global leader in outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services. With a strong track record of innovation, a broad and diverse geographic footprint and solid partnerships with lead customers, Amkor delivers high-quality solutions that enable the world's leading semiconductor and electronics companies to bring advanced technologies to market. The company's comprehensive portfolio includes advanced packaging, wafer-level processing, and system-in-package solutions targeting applications for smartphones, data centers, artificial intelligence, automobiles and wearables. For more information visit amkor.com .

Broadcom-TOPPAN JV Opens Singapore FC-BGA Substrate Facility for AI Chip Production
Article By : Stephen Las Marias 
Category : Packaging 
2026-10-21 
(0) Comments
Ask question of embedded
AST's 95,000-square-meter plant will produce large-body, high-layer-count substrates for AI computing and networking chips. 
Advanced Substrate Technologies (AST), a joint venture between TOPPAN Holdings Inc. and Broadcom Inc., has opened a manufacturing facility in Singapore for high-end flip-chip ball grid array (FC-BGA) substrates. It is the first facility of its kind in Singapore and TOPPAN Group’s first outside Japan.
Located in the Jurong Lake District, the facility will complement TOPPAN’s main production hub in Niigata, Japan. It is designed to manufacture large-body, high-layer-count substrates used in advanced semiconductor devices, including AI computing and networking chips.
“AST’s ability to deliver large-body, high-layer-count substrates at TOPPAN’s exacting standard is helping meet a real bottleneck in AI and networking chip production. We are grateful for the longstanding support and partnership of the Singapore government in this venture. This investment reflects both TOPPAN and Broadcom’s long-term commitment to Singapore as a critical hub in our global manufacturing network and strengthens the resilience of the semiconductor supply chain,” said Yoshiyuki Iida, CEO of AST, in a statement.
【Download】Transforming Healthcare with High Performance and Adaptive Computing 
Construction began in March 2024. AST has since recruited more than 200 engineers and skilled technicians, alongside operational staff. The site also includes R&D capabilities and will work with Singapore technology institutions on future substrate requirements.
The approximately 95,000-square-metre plant incorporates solar panels and water-recycling technologies. AST is targeting the start of high-value manufacturing by late 2026, with recruitment continuing across engineering and technical roles.
“Singapore continues to be an attractive destination and gateway to the global semiconductor industry for us, especially with a strong ecosystem of innovation, capabilities and resources. TOPPAN looks forward to continuing to drive advanced semiconductor packaging forward as artificial intelligence accelerates across the board,” said Satoshi Oya, President and COO of TOPPAN Holdings.
Singapore’s Economic Development Board (EDB) and JTC Corp. supported the project. EDB said the facility would expand the country’s advanced substrate capabilities and create jobs, while JTC highlighted the need for infrastructure to support next-generation semiconductor manufacturing.
As TOPPAN’s largest customer for FC-BGA substrates, Broadcom supported the facility’s development to secure additional capacity for its AI computing and networking products.
“AST’s FC-BGA substrate capacity in Singapore gives us meaningful flexibility and differentiation as demand for AI and networking silicon continues to climb. This facility, brought online three months early, strengthens our supply chain resilience by delivering vital relief while the industry is constrained by substrate shortages. Thanks to the exceptional execution by TOPPAN and AST, alongside the continued partnership of the Singapore EDB, this facility will deliver the next generation of large-body, high-layer-count substrates that Broadcom requires to further scale global AI infrastructure,” said Charlie Kawwas, President of Broadcom’s Semiconductor Solutions Group, in a press release.
AST plans to scale production with TOPPAN and Broadcom as demand for advanced substrates grows across AI, networking and next-generation computing.

title: HyProMag USA deploys third mobile system - Recycling Today
