content_text:
HyProMag USA deploys third mobile system
Several technology and recycling firms in the United States and Canada have collaborated to invest in mobile systems to process printed circuit boards and hard drives.
“The deployment of our third Inserma system as a mobile processing unit represents an important step in the development of the Dallas-Fort Worth project,” says Julian Treger, CEO of CoTec Holdings.
Photo courtesy of Intelligent Lifecycle Solutions 
By
Brian Taylor, Senior Editor 
Published October 20, 2026
Listen to article 
/ 
A coalition of firms in the United States and Canada, some with ownership stakes in each other, have now deployed three mobile hard disk drive (HDD) separation system designed to recover rare earth element (REE) and magnet materials from discarded electronic components.
Canada-based Mkango Magnetic Materials Ltd. says HyProMag USA LLC, in which it owns a stake, has announced the deployment of its third Spanish-made Inserma Anoia S.L. HDD separation system to be used as a mobile processing unit, “expanding HyProMag USA’s processing and customer engagement capabilities across the U.S.”
Adds Mkango, “The deployment further strengthens HyProMag USA’s partnership with Intelligent Lifecycle Solutions (ILS) and supports the expansion of a scalable nationwide platform for the recovery and recycling of rare earth magnets from end-of-life HDDs.”
ILS is based in Nevada and has processing capacity there and in South Carolina, according to Mkango.
Also involved is HyProMag USA co-owner CoTec Holdings Corp., a Canada-based firm that says it “integrates breakthrough technologies with strategic assets to unlock secure, sustainable, and low-cost supply chains.” 
Mkango says feedstock inventories currently under contract and in storage, together with active procurement programs undertaken by the companies involved, “continue to strengthen the feedstock platform and are expected to support initial commissioning and ramp-up activities” at a planned HyProMag USA Texas Hub facility in the Dallas-Fort Worth scheduled to open in 2028.
The Canadian company says Delaware-based HyProMag USA also has completed commercial sales of recovered printed circuit board (PCB) material to downstream smelter partners, generating revenue that supports the acquisition and retention of magnet-bearing feedstock inventory.
“The deployment of our third Inserma system as a mobile processing unit represents an important step in the development of the Dallas-Fort Worth project,” says Julian Treger, CEO of CoTec Holdings.
“Together with continued progress in feedstock sourcing and commercial PCB recovery, it strengthens our operating platform and expands our ability to engage directly with customers across multiple end markets,” adds Treger.
Remars Graham Davy, Managing Director of ILS , “The focus of the ILS team has been on demonstrating that HDDs can be efficiently processed into separate, marketable material streams. The mobile unit allows us to work directly with customers at their facilities, supporting trial programs, demonstrating material recovery performance and creating opportunities to secure additional feedstock supply.”
The companies say they are tapping into diversified feedstock channels “across industrial, health care, government and IT asset disposition sectors.”

title: GE HEALTHCARE LAUNCHES CELL DIVE FOR MORE PRECISE CELL BIOMARKER ANALYSIS - GE Healthcare
content_text:
GE HEALTHCARE LAUNCHES CELL DIVE FOR MORE PRECISE CELL BIOMARKER ANALYSIS
September 26, 2019
Developed by scientists for scientists – first patent issued 2009 for this product Flexibility of system allows for custom biomarker panel design and whole slide imaging Precise image registration enables spatial and quantititative biomarker analysis
(Paris, France and Seattle, Washington) September 26, 2019 - GE Healthcare launches Cell DIVE™ multiplexed imaging , an anti-body based solution that builds on years of research and development to transform immuno-oncology.
“Cell DIVE multiplexed imaging is another example of our commitment to furthering access to life-changing biotherapeutics and diagnostics, ” says Emmanuel Abate, General Manager Genomics and Cellular Research, GE Healthcare Life Sciences. “These are exciting days in immuno-oncology and we are early in our understanding in how a patient’s biomarker profile contributes to a therapeutic outcome.”
This technology was developed by scientists for scientists. The seminal work started in 2008 and the first patent was issued in 2009. Over the last decade, Cell DIVE has been evaluated globally through multiple collaborators resulting in a library of publications, presentations, and research . The milestone paper, Gerdes et al, (2013) in PNAS describes the ‘quantification and visualization of heterogeneous patterns of mTOR/MAPK signaling proteins’ – tackling challenges in tumor heterogeneity. All of this work brings us to the present moment with 400 validated commercially-available antibodies and a robust solution reaching the market.
“The flexibility of an open system that allows for custom biomarker panel design moves us closer to a definitive diagnostic tool,” says Prachi Bogetto, Diagnostics Segment Leader, GE Healthcare Life Sciences. “This flexible solution also supports whole slide, region of interest and tissue microarray (TMA) imaging.”
At its core, scientists will iteratively probe, image, and de-stain to capture thousands of spatial cellular data points from just one tissue image. With our extensive list of validated antibodies, scientists can customize their own panels and have the flexibility to stain and image as they need. Scientists can have confidence knowing that our gentle protocol won’t harm the tissue sample. No stripping of antibodies or complicated sample prep required. GE Healthcare continued its commitment to quality by ensuring this technology produces high quality image data through accurate registration and stitching technology.
Female, Age 41, Lung, Adenocarcinoma, (DAPI blue;AKT Green;EGFR Red; pEGFR Aqua; pERK yellow; HER 2 Magenta)
The Cell DIVE multiplexed imaging solution is commercially available now.

Sumitomo Chemical works with Tata
20th October 2026
Submitted by:
Andrew Warmington
Sumitomo Chemical has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with India’s Tata Electronics to explore a possible collaboration in semiconductor fabrication. The company will examine specific measures aimed at establishing a stable supply system for materials, possibly including a semiconductor chemicals facility in India.
Sumitomo Chemical’s ICT & Mobility Solutions sector is one of its growth drivers and the semiconductor materials business has been designated as a priority area within it. The business offers advanced photoresists and semiconductor chemicals, being particularly known for high-purity chemicals.
In recent years, Sumitomo Chemical has expanded its semiconductor chemicals capacity in Japan and South Korea, while establishing a new base in Texas. Earlier this year, it acquired Asia Union Electronic Chemical, with facilities in Taiwan and Nevada. It has also begun operations at advanced high-purity chemical centres in Japan and South Korea to develop new processes and recycling technologies.
Another Japanese player, Nissan Chemical, has separately established a wholly-owned subsidiary in Zhangjiagang in China’s Jiangsu province. This will make anti-reflective coatings for the photoresists and multilayer materials used in semiconductors. The company said that demand for semiconductors in China has continued to expand, driven by ongoing digitalisation and other factors, whilecustomer demand for supply chain resilience has grown.

title: AdapTronics wins Infineon’s humanoid robotics startup challenge - Electronics Weekly
query: ("Infineon" OR "Infineon Technologies") (Korea OR Korean) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
AdapTronics wins Infineon’s humanoid robotics startup challenge
by 
David Manners 
20th October 2026 
in 
Business , News 
0 
AdapTronics from Italy has won the Infineon Startup Challenge 2026 focused on key technologies for humanoid robots. COSMOKE of Korea was runner up and TECHiFAB from Germany third.
The three winning teams are pictured above.
AdapTronics won with an innovative gripping technology for humanoid robots. “The challenge gave us valuable access to technology experts, industry insights and a strong innovation network. We look forward to further advancing our solution and exploring new opportunities for collaboration,” says Lorenzo Agostini, founder and CEO of AdapTronics.
COSMOKE from South Korea was in second place with its magnetic tactile sensing technology for physical AI – COSKIN – which enables humanoid robots to perceive touch, pressure, and physical interactions.
TECHiFAB from Germany came third with its In-Memory Computing based approach to real-time motor control for robotic actuators. This is physical AI by definition and is designed to enable faster, more energy-efficient and safer control while improving performance directly within the drive train of humanoid robots.
Over 100 startups from 29 countries participated in the challenge, 15 were selected to pitch their solutions enabling the next generation of humanoid robots and physical AI applications to an international jury
The programme provided access to Infineon technologies, expert mentoring, business coaching, and an international innovation network
Following four months of intensive collaboration, development and mentoring, 15 selected startups out of more than 100 applicants presented their solutions at the Infineon Startup Challenge Demo Day, held during the Electronic Based Systems Conference (EBSCON) in Graz, Austria.
The challenge brought together startups from Europe and Asia, investors, industry experts and technology leaders to advance innovation in robotics and physical AI.
Participants developed solutions that enable humanoid robots to better perceive and interact with their environment, manipulate objects, and perform precise movements.
The winners were selected by an international jury comprising experts from industry, venture capital, startup ecosystems, and technology innovation.
“Strategic collaboration with startups creates a win-win situation, combining novel ideas with industrially proven semiconductor technologies and thereby accelerating innovative, market-ready applications,” says Infineon svp Sören Jehmlich, “the Startup Challenge is a key pillar of our innovation culture.”
The solutions presented during the challenge reflect the technologies required for the next generation of humanoid robots, from tactile sensing to dexterous gripping and precise motor control.
To support the startups in developing and validating their concepts, Infineon provided access to dedicated hardware and software platforms, including Environmental Sensing Kits, Artificial Skin Kits, Motor Control Kits, Visual Feedback Kits, and in-house AI development software, enabling teams to accelerate prototyping and transform innovative ideas into scalable applications.
“Humanoid robots are the most complex form of physical AI and highly relevant for Infineon,” said Dirk Geiger, Senior Director & Team Lead Humanoid Robotics at Infineon. “They combine power, sensing, real-time connectivity, safety and security with software and AI compute, turning machines into autonomous systems. No single company can master this complexity alone. With the Startup Challenge, we gave startups early access to our hardware stack as well as our software and system offering and brought them together with our partners and application experts. The solutions shown prove how quickly ideas can become building blocks for scalable humanoid platforms and give valuable insight into where the technology is heading.”
The Infineon Startup Challenge is part of the global Infineon Startup Co-Innovation Program, in which Infineon collaborates with startups as a technology and development partner.
As the winner of the Infineon Startup Challenge 2026, AdapTronics will now join the Infineon Startup Co-Innovation Program to further develop and scale its solution together with Infineon.
The collaboration will officially kick off at the Startup Night in Munich in November, where Infineon showcases successful startup partnerships and highlights the value of startup-driven innovation.
Infineon continues to engage with other promising participants for future technological and business collaboration. By combining the agility and creativity of startups with Infineon’s technological expertise and global capabilities, the program supports the development of scalable applications and accelerates innovation in humanoid robotics and physical AI.

MODULAR LOGO SYSTEM UNIFIES MAXON’S CREATIVE SOFTWARE layout
 
Motion designer Casey Gu creates the Maxon One Brand Expression Film to introduce a unified visual identity across Maxon’s suite of creative tools. The project translates a modular logo system into motion, establishing a visual connection between products spanning 2D and 3D design, motion graphics, and visual effects. Rather than treating each product as an isolated identity, the film explores how distinct visual characteristics can coexist within a shared brand framework.
 
Led by Leo Hageman, Director of Brand & Creative, the new identity brings together Maxon One, Cinema 4D, Red Giant, ZBrush, Redshift, Universe, Capsules, Cinebench, Cineware, and Moves through a consistent geometric language. Its modular, honeycomb-inspired forms provide the structural basis for this relationship, creating continuity across a diverse range of tools while maintaining room for individual product identities.
all images ©Casey Gu  
 
motion design balances abstract geometry with brand motifs
 
For motion designer Casey Gu, the central challenge was translating the modular visual system into motion while balancing abstraction with product recognition. Using geometric forms, unique transitions, and rhythmic movement, Casey developed a visual narrative that highlights the signature features of each tool while maintaining a consistent visual language across the ecosystem.
 
The animated sequences extend the logo system beyond static marks, using movement to express both individual product identities and their relationships within the broader suite. Shared geometric elements establish continuity, while variations in composition and motion reflect the different functions of each tool. Together, these elements create a flexible visual framework that connects Maxon’s products without diminishing their individual identities.

Qualcomm Showcases V2X Technology at 2026 Gangneung ITS World Congress
Demonstrations include scalable V2X, ADAS integration and global V2X solutions
JEONG IL JOO 
Published 2026.10.19 19:10
Reply 0

가

Qualcomm showcases V2X-based traffic safety technologies and solutions at the 2026 Gangneung ITS World Congress. (Photo: Qualcomm) 
Qualcomm announced on Oct. 19 that it will showcase traffic safety technologies and solutions based on vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communications at the 2026 ITS World Congress in Gangneung, South Korea.
The ITS World Congress is an event focused on intelligent transportation system policies, technologies and services. It addresses future mobility issues, including connected vehicles, autonomous driving, smart infrastructure and artificial intelligence (AI). This year’s event runs from Oct. 19 to 23 at Gangneung Olympic Park in Gangwon Province.
Qualcomm will demonstrate seven technologies during the event and exhibit real-world applications. These include scalable V2X, advanced driver assistance system (ADAS)-based V2X, smart infrastructure, global V2X solutions and products developed by partners using Qualcomm technologies.
V2X enables vehicles to exchange wireless data directly with other vehicles, road infrastructure, pedestrians, motorcycles and other surrounding objects. Using radio signals, the technology can identify potential hazards and warn drivers even in blind spots or adverse weather conditions where visibility is limited. Conventional camera and radar sensors have been limited to detecting obstacles directly ahead or objects within their line of sight.
Scalable V2X allows communication capabilities and data processing levels to be adjusted flexibly according to driving conditions and vehicle performance.
ADAS-based V2X combines onboard sensor systems with V2X communications. Rather than simply warning drivers of potential hazards, the technology enables vehicles to initiate automatic emergency braking (AEB) or steering control.
Qualcomm Korea President Kim Sang-pyo delivers a keynote speech titled “Accelerating Innovation in Traffic Safety.” (Photo: Qualcomm) 
Smart infrastructure refers to intelligent road environments equipped with communication modules and detection sensors installed in traffic lights, electronic road signs, streetlights and base stations.
Global V2X refers to V2X solutions based on worldwide standards.
Kim Sang-pyo, president of Qualcomm Korea, delivered a keynote speech titled “Accelerating Innovation in Traffic Safety.”
“Qualcomm has led mobile communications technology for more than 40 years and has worked with numerous partners to advance the V2X ecosystem, from standardization to commercialization,” Kim said. “We are supporting the development of safe and intelligent transportation systems that reflect real-world road conditions in South Korea.”

Terafab reportedly to receive first ASML EUV scanner in mid-2027
19 October 2026 
Paul van Gerven 
Editor at Bits&Chips
Reading time: 1 minute
Elon Musk’s Terafab is expected to receive its first ASML EUV lithography system in mid-2027, according to journalist Tim Culpan , citing sources familiar with the matter. The scanner could arrive before the research fab near Austin is ready to accommodate it. Semianalysis expects equipment installation to begin later that year.
Credit: Terafab 
The reported delivery suggests Terafab will initially use conventional EUV equipment despite Musk’s public enthusiasm for free-electron laser light sources. Introducing an alternative light source would likely add too much process development and equipment qualification work.
Separately, Terafab’s planned volume-production site is being developed in Grimes County, Texas. Semianalysis forecasts that the first phase will begin operating in late 2029 and reach volume production by mid-2030. The fab reportedly plans to adopt Intel’s 14A process.

Qualcomm showcases V2X in Gangneung, pledges Korea smart traffic cooperation 
Qualcomm touts real-time V2X safety demos in Gangneung, vows deeper Korea-focused deployments 
입력 2026.10.19. 16:47 
조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 
Qualcomm showcased vehicle-to-everything (V2X) technology that consolidates vehicles, road infrastructure, and pedestrians in real time at the 2026 Gangneung Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS) World Congress, which opened on the 19th.
Kim Sang-pyo, Qualcomm Korea president/Courtesy of Qualcomm Korea 
Qualcomm said on the 19th it will exhibit V2X-based traffic safety solutions and related products at the event being held in Gangneung through the 23rd.
V2X is a technology in which a vehicle communicates with other vehicles, road facilities such as traffic lights, and pedestrians to understand surrounding traffic conditions. Unlike cameras or radar, it can also deliver risk information from areas not directly visible, helping prevent accidents that can occur in blind spots at intersections or beyond sensor detection ranges.
At this event, Qualcomm is introducing extended V2X, V2X linked with advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), smart road infrastructure, and global V2X solutions. It is also exhibiting partner products that apply Qualcomm technology.
In particular, it is presenting use cases that combine vehicle sensors and communication technology to identify the movements of surrounding vehicles and pedestrians and issue early warnings of dangerous situations. The company said this can supplement the limitations of existing vehicle sensors and improve road safety and traffic operations efficiency.
On the day, Kim Sang-pyo, president of Qualcomm Korea, delivered a keynote speech on the theme of accelerating traffic safety innovation. Kim said, "For more than 40 years, Qualcomm has contributed to the development of the global ecosystem from V2X standardization to commercialization and real-world road deployment, based on the technological expertise accumulated in the mobile consolidation field."
Kim added, "In Korea, we are also supporting the establishment of safe and intelligent transportation systems through interoperability verification that reflects actual road environments," and said, "Going forward, we will enhance road safety and expand the possibilities of future mobility based on consolidation technology."
Meanwhile, the congress, hosted and organized by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, Gangneung City, and ITS KOREA, is being held under the theme of "A world united beyond mobility." Government, industry, and academic stakeholders from various countries are participating to discuss policies and technologies related to intelligent transport systems and to conduct demonstrations of advanced transport technologies.

HYPROMAG USA DEPLOYS MOBILE INSERMA SYSTEM, EXTENDING HDD PROCESSING TO CUSTOMER SITES ACROSS THE UNITED STATES 
Feedstock platform continues to build ahead of Dallas-Fort Worth commissioning, with commercial PCB sales to smelter partners generating revenue that supports magnet acquisition 
LONDON / VANCOUVER: 19 October 2026 – Mkango Magnetic Materials Ltd. (AIM/TSX-V: MKA) (“Mkango”) is pleased to announce that HyProMag USA LLC (“HyProMag USA”) has announced the deployment of its third Inserma Anoia S.L. (“Inserma”) hard disk drive (“HDD”) separation system as a mobile processing unit, expanding HyProMag USA's processing and customer engagement capabilities across the United States. The deployment further strengthens HyProMag USA's partnership [1] with Intelligent Lifecycle Solutions (“ ILS”) and supports the expansion of a scalable nationwide platform for the recovery and recycling of rare earth magnets from end-of-life HDDs. 
Feedstock inventories currently under contract and in storage, together with active procurement programs, continue to strengthen the feedstock platform and are expected to support initial commissioning and ramp-up activities for Phase 1 at the planned Dallas-Fort Worth facility (the “Texas Hub”) in 2028. HyProMag USA has also completed commercial sales of recovered printed circuit board (“PCB”) material to downstream smelter partners, generating revenue that supports the acquisition and retention of magnet-bearing feedstock inventory. 
Julian Treger, Chief Executive Officer of CoTec Holdings Corp. (“CoTec”), commented : “The deployment of our third Inserma system as a mobile processing unit represents an important step in the development of the Dallas-Fort Worth project. Together with continued progress in feedstock sourcing and commercial PCB recovery, it strengthens our operating platform and expands our ability to engage directly with customers across multiple end markets. These milestones provide increasing confidence in our ability to support commissioning activities and establish a long-term domestic supply of recycled rare earth materials.” 
Graham Davy, Managing Director of ILS, commented: “The focus of the ILS team has been on demonstrating that HDDs can be efficiently processed into separate, marketable material streams. We have continued to build feedstock inventories, completed commercial sales of recovered PCB materials to smelter partners for HyProMag USA and expanded our capabilities through the deployment of a mobile Inserma system. The mobile unit allows us to work directly with customers at their facilities, supporting trial programs, demonstrating material recovery performance and creating opportunities to secure additional feedstock supply.” 
Key Highlights 
● Processing capability expanded: HyProMag USA's third Inserma HDD separation system has been deployed as a mobile processing unit to support customer qualification programs, secure on-site recovery campaigns and future feedstock growth opportunities across the United States. 
● Commissioning readiness advanced: Feedstock inventories currently under contract and in storage, together with active procurement programs, are expected to support initial commissioning and ramp-up of Phase 1 activities at the Texas Hub in 2028. 
● PCB revenue supports magnet acquisition: Commercial sales of recovered PCB material to smelter partners have generated revenue within the HDD processing flow sheet, partly offsetting the cost of acquiring and retaining magnet-bearing feedstock for future rare earth recycling operations. 
● Feedstock channels diversified: Sourcing activities continue to expand across industrial, healthcare, government and IT asset disposition sectors. 
● Secure processing platform: R2v3-certified operations, ISO-certified management systems and documented chain-of-custody procedures support secure handling of data-bearing equipment. 
● Data center market focus: Mobile processing capability enables on-site recovery programs within hyperscale data centers and secure IT asset disposition environments. 
● Inserma testing: A next generation Inserma system designed specifically for the high-capacity HDDs used in hyperscale data centers, including helium filled units, is currently being tested, with early results indicating processing times of under three seconds per drive and successful processing of modern high-capacity data center formats. 
● Partnership network expanding: Relationships across the data center, electronics recycling and rare earth magnet value chain continue to support platform growth. 
Expanding Feedstock Access 
To support continued growth in feedstock volumes, HyProMag USA has deployed its third Inserma HDD separation system as a mobile processing unit to complement existing operations in South Carolina and Nevada. Unlike the fixed installations currently operating through the ILS partnership, the system has been configured for mobile deployment and is intended to support customer trials, feedstock development programs and on-site processing campaigns across the United States. 
Feedstock inventories currently under contract and in storage, together with active procurement programs, continue to strengthen the feedstock platform and are expected to support initial commissioning and ramp-up activities at the Texas Hub. Feedstock sourcing activities continue to expand beyond HDDs into industrial, healthcare, government and IT asset disposition sectors, increasing confidence in the scalability of HyProMag USA's feedstock platform and supporting future supply requirements for the Texas Hub. 
Commercial PCB Recovery 
ILS has completed commercial sales for HyProMag USA of recovered PCB material to downstream smelter partners. The sales validate an additional revenue stream within the HDD processing flow sheet and show that value can be recovered from secondary material streams. Magnet-bearing materials are being retained as feedstock inventory for future rare earth recycling operations. Revenue from recovered PCB material partly offsets the cost of acquiring magnet-bearing feedstock, improving the economics of building the inventory required to support Texas Hub operations. 
Secure Recovery and Chain of Custody 
ILS operates under internationally recognized recycling and management standards, including R2v3 certification and ISO-certified management systems, supporting responsible recycling practices, operational controls and continuous improvement initiatives. The recovery process is supported by documented chain-of-custody procedures designed to provide traceability from collection through processing and final disposition. These controls support the requirements of data center operators, IT asset disposition providers, enterprise customers and government organizations seeking secure and auditable management of end-of-life electronic equipment. 
Building Strategic Partnerships 
HyProMag USA continues to expand relationships across the electronics recycling, data infrastructure and rare earth magnet value chain. Working alongside data center operators, IT asset disposition providers, recyclers, technology companies and downstream processing partners, HyProMag USA is developing an integrated platform for the collection, recovery and recycling of magnet-bearing materials. HyProMag USA is evaluating additional feedstock pathways, including industrial and transportation-related material streams, with pilot programs and commercial opportunities under review. 
About ILS 
Intelligent Lifecycle Solutions (“ILS”) provides secure recovery, processing and recycling services for end-of-life electronic equipment. Through its operating facilities in South Carolina and Nevada, ILS supports the recovery of valuable materials from electronic waste streams while maintaining robust data security and chain-of-custody protocols. 
About HyProMag USA 
HyProMag USA is developing advanced rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing operations to establish a secure domestic U.S. supply chain for neodymium iron boron (“NdFeB”) magnets, essential components for AI infrastructure, defense systems, robotics, electric vehicles, and advanced electronics. Leveraging the revolutionary Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap (“HPMS”) technology, developed over 15 years with over US$100 million in R&D investment, HyProMag USA delivers faster magnet-to-magnet short-loop recycling that uses 88% less energy and reduces carbon emissions by 85% compared to conventional methods. HPMS accepts a wide range of magnet-bearing feedstocks – including end-of-life EV motors, data-center and industrial equipment, consumer electronics, and manufacturing scrap – enabling recovery of magnet-grade material without chemical processing. 
Ownership 
HyProMag USA LLC is owned 50:50 by CoTec Holdings Corp. (TSXV: CTH; OTCQX: CTHCF) (“CoTec”) and HyProMag Limited. HyProMag Limited is 100% owned by Maginito Limited which is owned on a 79.4%/20.6% basis by Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited (AIM/TSX-V: MKA) and CoTec. 
About Mkango Magnetic Materials Ltd. 
Mkango is listed on the AIM and the TSX-V Stock Exchanges. Mkango’s corporate strategy is to become a market leader in the production of recycled rare earth magnets, alloys and oxides, through its interest in Maginito Limited (“Maginito”), which is owned 79.4 per cent by Mkango and 20.6 per cent by CoTec Holdings Corp. (“CoTec”), and the Remloy business acquired by its wholly owned German subsidiary, to develop new sustainable sources of neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium to supply accelerating demand from electric vehicles, wind turbines and other clean energy technologies. 
Maginito holds a 100 per cent interest in HyProMag Limited and a 90 per cent direct and indirect interest (assuming conversion of Maginito’s convertible loan) in HyProMag GmbH, focused on short loop rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing in the UK and Germany, respectively, and a 100 per cent interest in Mkango Rare Earths UK Ltd (“Mkango UK”), focused on long loop rare earth magnet recycling in the UK via a chemical processing route. 
Maginito and CoTec are also expanding Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap (“HPMS”) recycling technology into the United States via the 50/50 owned HyProMag USA joint venture company. 
Remloy has developed a plant in Bitterfeld, Germany, which recycles end-of-life rare earth magnets via a melting process (medium loop rare earth magnet recycling) to produce NdFeB alloy powders for the bonded and hot deformed magnet markets, complementary to HyProMag’s short loop recycling process, to produce sintered magnets, and to Mkango UK’s long loop recycling process, to produce mixed rare earth carbonates and oxides. 
Mkango currently owns 100% of the advanced stage Songwe Hill rare earths project in Malawi and the proposed Pulawy rare earths separation plant in Poland. On grant of the large-scale mining licence the Government of Malawi may elect to take a free 10% interest in the entity holding that licence. The Songwe and Pulawy projects and HyProMag GmbH have been selected as Strategic Projects under the European Union Critical Raw Materials Act. Songwe has also received Development Funding from the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (“DFC”), the U.S. Government’s development finance institution, securing US$4.6 million in reimbursable funding for Front End Engineering and Design. Mkango Rare Earths Limited (“MKAR”) has signed a Business Combination Agreement with Crown PropTech Acquisitions (“CPTK”) to list the Songwe Hill and Pulawy rare earths projects on NASDAQ via a SPAC merger (the “Proposed Business Combination”) under the name Mkango Rare Earths Limited.

content_text:
Equipment giants are vying for advanced packaging
半导体行业观察 2026-10-19 10:59 
Today, the competition among equipment vendors centering on hybrid bonding is essentially an early strategic layout for the dominance of the future 3D integrated manufacturing process. 
In early October, a piece of news in the capital market drew widespread attention: over concerns that ASML may enter the hybrid bonding equipment market and the demand for HBM-related equipment will be postponed, Bank of America downgraded the investment rating of Besi, a Dutch packaging equipment manufacturer, on October 6, driving its share price down 5.39% on the same day; the next day, as UBS further downgraded its rating, Besi's share price fell another 8.49%, with a cumulative drop of about 13.4% in just two trading days. In fact, ASML delivered the TWINSCAN XT:260 lithography system for advanced packaging as early as 2025, and news of its R&D of hybrid bonding equipment came out this year, further expanding its business beyond traditional lithography.
Overview of Besi's stock price trend (Source: Yahoo)
Meanwhile, Applied Materials and Lam Research are also accelerating their layout. In the first week of October alone, Applied Materials successively announced deepened cooperation with Besi and Intel, with R&D scope covering hybrid bonding, TCB, chip-to-panel, Foveros 3D packaging and other technologies. Leveraging technologies such as etching, deposition and copper electroplating, Lam Research continues to expand its equipment layout in the fields of TSV and 3D interconnection. In March this year, Reuters reported that both Lam Research and Applied Materials showed acquisition interest in Besi.
It can be seen that the three giants of front-end equipment are extending to advanced packaging along different technical routes. On the one hand, the front-end equipment giants are actively extending to advanced packaging, and on the other hand, the traditional leading packaging equipment manufacturers have become the targets of cooperation, investment and even potential mergers and acquisitions. The originally relatively clear division of labor between front-end and back-end in the semiconductor equipment industry is undergoing subtle changes. Advanced packaging is becoming a new battlefield that semiconductor equipment giants are vying to enter. 
The Three Front-End Equipment Giants Are Surrounding Advanced Packaging 
In fact, a closer look shows that although Applied Materials, Lam Research and ASML are all extending to the advanced packaging field, the three have chosen different entry methods.
Applied Materials pays more attention to material engineering and process integration, and builds comprehensive solutions covering multiple manufacturing links by cooperating with professional packaging equipment manufacturers; Lam Research relies on etching, deposition and copper interconnection technologies to compete for more and more key process steps in the 3D integration process; ASML has begun to try to extend its accumulated nanoscale motion control, precision alignment and measurement technologies in the lithography field to hybrid bonding equipment.
These three routes are complementary to each other, and may gradually form direct competition as technology evolves.
Applied Materials: Join hands with Besi to build a complete process chain
First of all, talking about Applied Materials, its layout in advanced packaging has actually lasted for many years.
As early as 2020, Applied Materials and Besi established a joint R&D project in Singapore, combining its own technologies in etching, planarization, thin film deposition, wafer cleaning, metrology and inspection, and particle control with Besi's capabilities in precision chip mounting, interconnection and assembly.
The representative achievement of the cooperation between the two parties is the Kinex integrated Die-to-Wafer (D2W) hybrid bonding system. Different from traditional packaging equipment that mainly focuses on chip mounting and connection, Kinex attempts to integrate pre-bonding processes such as surface treatment, cleaning, activation and alignment into a more compact manufacturing flow.
Kinex (Image source: Applied Materials)
This design has practical significance.
In the hybrid bonding process, the two chips or wafers to be connected must not only achieve extremely high-precision geometric alignment, but also ensure the flatness, cleanliness and material state of the bonding surface. Even if the bonding equipment itself has excellent positioning accuracy, if the previous process causes particle pollution, abnormal copper pad depression or unstable surface state, it may still lead to connection defects. The cooperation between Applied Materials and Besi is essentially an attempt to combine traditional front-end material engineering with back-end precision assembly technology to improve the final yield through cross-process collaboration.
It is worth noting that Applied Materials does not limit technical cooperation to Besi alone. Previously, it also cooperated with EV Group (EVG), an Austrian wafer bonding equipment manufacturer, to develop wafer-to-wafer bonding solutions.
The cooperation upgrade on October 1 this year further expanded the R&D boundary of both parties. According to the official announcement, Besi will become an innovation partner of Applied Materials' EPIC R&D center located in Silicon Valley. In the future, the two parties will not only continue to promote D2W hybrid bonding, but also jointly research TCB process scaling, chip-to-chip, chip-to-panel and new integration architectures for optical interconnection. The EPIC center is planned to have a maximum investment scale of about 5 billion US dollars, and the investment will be gradually rolled out as customer projects advance. An important goal of this center is to enable chip manufacturers, equipment suppliers and material enterprises to participate in joint R&D at an earlier stage, shortening the cycle for new processes to move from the laboratory to mass production.
From the perspective of industrial significance, this means that Applied Materials is trying to incorporate advanced packaging, which was previously a relatively independent back-end manufacturing link, into its broader material engineering R&D system.
Just five days later, Applied Materials announced the deepening of cooperation with Intel, covering R&D of next-generation transistors, on-chip interconnection and Foveros 3D advanced packaging.
These two cooperations seem to target different enterprises, but their technical logic is connected. In 3D stacking, there are complex interactions between interconnection density, power supply paths, heat dissipation structures and material stress between chips. The performance optimization of next-generation chips is increasingly difficult to achieve by relying solely on one link among advanced process, metal interconnection or packaging.
Therefore, for Applied Materials, the real strategic value may not only be to obtain more orders for hybrid bonding equipment, but to participate in the definition of next-generation chip manufacturing processes earlier through the joint development of front-end and back-end processes. As Prabu Raja from Applied Materials asserted: Advanced packaging is no longer just the physical assembly of the back-end, but a material engineering revolution that requires wafer-level precision and cleanliness.
Lam Research: From Etching, Deposition to 3D Interconnection 
Compared with the cooperation model between Applied Materials and Besi, Lam Research's layout in the advanced packaging field highlights its existing process and equipment advantages. Lam Research has accumulated a large number of high-aspect-ratio etching, thin film deposition and metal interconnection technologies in the past in the manufacture of logic chips, DRAM and 3D NAND.
With the continuous 3D development of advanced packaging, these technologies are gaining more application scenarios. For example, in 3D stacked chips, Through-Silicon Vias (TSVs) undertake vertical electrical connections between different chip layers. To make deep and narrow vias in silicon wafers, high-aspect-ratio etching technology is required, and the via sidewall morphology, etching uniformity and defect control should be guaranteed as much as possible.
Lam Research's Syndion deep reactive ion etching equipment is designed for deep hole etching requirements including TSV. But etching the via is only the first step. After forming the insulating layer, barrier layer and seed layer, the via needs to be filled by metal deposition to form a reliable electrical connection. If voids, seams or other defects occur during the copper filling process, it may affect resistance, heat dissipation and long-term reliability.
The SABRE 3D copper electroplating platform that Lam Research highlighted in July this year is developed around the manufacturing needs of complex metal interconnection in advanced packaging. The company emphasizes that as the interconnection structure of advanced packaging becomes more and more refined, the requirements for metal filling uniformity and void control in the manufacturing process are continuously increasing. SABRE 3D provides metal filling capabilities for structures such as TSV, wafer-level packaging and redistribution layers through electrochemical deposition processes.
In addition, Lam Research has also deployed the VECTOR TEOS 3D dielectric material deposition equipment, as well as related wet and deposition processes for large-sized substrates.
It is worth noting that the attraction of advanced packaging to Lam Research is not just hybrid bonding itself. From traditional 2.5D packaging to 3D chip stacking, and then to panel-level packaging, more and more manufacturing steps require high-precision etching, thin film deposition and metal interconnection processes, which are the fields that Lam Research has long been deeply engaged in.
Therefore, Lam Research's competitive logic is not necessarily to directly replace Besi to manufacture bonding equipment, but to obtain more value in the advanced packaging industry chain by expanding the coverage of key process equipment.
However, the company's interest in bonding equipment is also worthy of attention. In March 2026, Reuters, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that Besi has attracted the attention of potential acquirers due to its hybrid bonding technology, and both Lam Research and Applied Materials are on the relevant list.
For Lam Research, if it wants to further expand into direct bonding equipment, leveraging professional equipment enterprises that already have a customer base and mass production experience may help it establish market position faster than relying entirely on internal R&D.
However, up to now, public reports have not confirmed that the relevant acquisition transaction has finally been reached. This also reveals some information: the next round of competition in the advanced packaging equipment industry may be accompanied by equity investment, strategic cooperation and even industrial integration in addition to technology R&D and product upgrading.
ASML: From Lithography to Hybrid Bonding, Directly Challenging Besi? 
It can be seen that the advanced packaging business of Applied Materials and Lam Research mainly stems from the horizontal extension of their existing material engineering capabilities. However, ASML's potential entry may have a more direct impact on the traditional hybrid bonding equipment market.
As the exclusive global supplier of EUV lithography equipment, ASML's core technical accumulation is concentrated in the fields of high-precision optics, motion control, wafer positioning, deformation compensation and nanoscale overlay accuracy.
In the past, these technologies were mainly used to accurately transfer increasingly tiny circuit patterns to the wafer surface. However, in hybrid bonding, there is also a very critical problem to be solved: how to accurately align the metal interconnection structures on two wafers or different chips and maintain stability during the bonding process. Therefore, there is a certain degree of commonality between ASML's original technical capabilities and hybrid bonding equipment. 
In fact, ASML has already entered the advanced packaging market through dedicated lithography equipment. At the annual general meeting of shareholders held in April 2026, ASML disclosed that the company has delivered the first TWINSCAN XT:260 i-line lithography system, which is specially designed for 3D integration and advanced packaging applications. Different from EUV scanners, which are mainly used for advanced logic processes, the XT:260 targets special patterning requirements in advanced packaging. ASML pointed out in its demonstration materials that the micro-bump process requires a large depth of focus, while hybrid bonding puts forward higher requirements for pattern resolution. This means that as the interconnection density of advanced packaging continues to increase, lithography itself has begun to become an important link affecting the evolution of packaging technology.
The TWINSCAN XT:260 launched by ASML last year is an i-line scanner that can process 270 wafers per hour. In view of the growing demand for AI chips, ASML plans to shift its business focus from pure front-end chip production equipment to packaging and bonding technologies in the next 10 to 15 years. (Image source: ASML)
But ASML is obviously not satisfied with only providing advanced packaging lithography equipment.
In March this year, South Korean media The Elec reported that ASML has started the overall architecture design of hybrid bonding equipment and has been in contact for cooperation with long-term suppliers such as Prodrive Technologies and VDL ETG. These enterprises previously participated in the supply of precision motion systems, drive devices and mechanical structures for ASML's lithography equipment. If ASML tries to transfer its accumulation in high-precision motion platforms to bonding equipment, it may further narrow the technical distance between lithography equipment and hybrid bonding equipment.
Moreover, there is another point worthy of attention that ASML has already published related patents.
The international patent WO2026098870A1 published on May 15, 2026 is titled "Bonding Apparatus", with the applicant being ASML Netherlands BV. The patent relates to a bonding device for two semiconductor substrates, focusing on discussing how to improve the alignment problem that may occur in the bonding process through state control of the substrate support surface. The patent document points out that factors such as internal stress of the wafer, support surface state and flatness may cause alignment deviation during bonding. This is obviously related to ASML's long-term research on wafer deformation compensation, position measurement and precision motion control technologies.
Of course, patent layout does not mean that mass-produced equipment is already mature. ASML has not yet publicly confirmed the commercial delivery time, customer certification progress or mass production performance of its hybrid bonding equipment. But this potential competition has begun to affect the market's expectations for traditional equipment enterprises. On October 6, Bank of America downgraded Besi's investment rating, which mentioned the competitive risk that ASML may enter the hybrid bonding market in the future.
For Besi, this risk is worthy of attention. In the traditional advanced packaging equipment market, Besi's important advantages come from long-term accumulation in precision mounting, assembly processes and hybrid bonding technology. Once ASML officially enters, it may form a new competitive force with its experience in nanoscale positioning, precision measurement and large-scale complex equipment system engineering.
However, from having key technical capabilities to developing competitive commercial equipment and then passing the mass production certification of wafer fabs, there is still a considerable long process of technology and commercialization.
Whether ASML can really challenge Besi ultimately depends on the alignment accuracy, throughput, yield, equipment stability, cost and customer certification progress of the equipment, and cannot be judged solely based on patents or supply chain news.
Why Has Hybrid Bonding Become the Focus of Competition? 
An important background for front-end equipment giants to enter advanced packaging one after another is that chip interconnection technology is changing.
In traditional 2.5D and 3D packaging, chips usually establish electrical connections through Micro-bumps. Thermal Compression Bonding (TCB) achieves reliable connection between solder and metal pads by applying temperature and pressure. This process is widely used in the field of high-performance computing and memory chips, but with the increase of chip stacking layers and the improvement of interconnection density, traditional micro-bump structures are gradually facing higher requirements in terms of pitch, connection height, parasitic effect and thermomechanical reliability.
Hybrid bonding provides another technical route. It combines direct dielectric bonding with metal interconnection to reduce the dependence on traditional solder bumps, thus making it possible to achieve smaller interconnection pitch, higher connection density and more compact chip stacking structure.
In May 2026, Imec, the Belgian microelectronics research center, and EV Group announced that they had achieved a 200nm copper interconnection pitch in wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding research. The research team achieved a post-bond copper pad overlay deviation of less than 40nm for all test chips on 300mm wafers.

Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany to Acquire Silence Therapeutics, Strengthening Rare Disease Pipeline with Innovative siRNA Asset 
We enter into a definitive agreement to acquire biotechnology company Silence Therapeutics, focused on siRNA-therapies in areas of high unmet need.

Icons revealed to the left 
19 Oct 2026 
| 
Darmstadt, Germany 
Purchase price of $20 per ADS in cash represents an enterprise value of $1.1 billion and an equity value of approximately $1.3 billion 
Silence Therapeutics is a UK-headquartered biotechnology company with a potentially best-in-class Phase 3-ready investigational siRNA therapy for rare disease, polycythemia vera (PV) 
Planned acquisition will strengthen the position of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany in rare diseases, a high-value growth driver, and advance its Healthcare ambition to become a leading Global Specialty Innovator 
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, a leading science and technology company, today announced its entry into a definitive agreement to acquire Silence Therapeutics plc (Nasdaq: SLN), a global clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in London, UK, focused on pioneering the design and development of siRNA (short interfering RNA) therapies in areas of high unmet need.
The purchase price of $20 per ADS in cash, with each ADS representing three ordinary shares of Silence Therapeutics (or $6.6667 per ordinary share), represents an enterprise value of $1.1 billion and an equity value of approximately $1.3 billion. The consideration represents an 82% premium to Silence Therapeutics’ 30-day volume-weighted average price of $10.99, as of the close of trading on October 16, 2026, the last trading day prior to the transaction announcement. The transaction is subject to satisfaction of customary closing conditions.
“The planned acquisition of Silence Therapeutics will strengthen our capabilities to serve patients with targeted specialty and rare diseases,” said Kai Beckmann, Chairman of the Executive Board and Group CEO of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany. “Following the acquisition of SpringWorks Therapeutics last year, we continue to transform our pipeline toward areas of high specialization and unmet medical need, with an ongoing commitment to external innovation. The proposed transaction follows our strategic priority to address attractive end markets also through M&A, creating value over the mid- to long-term.”
The transaction, once completed, will add Divesiran ─ a potentially best-in-class, phase 3-ready siRNA investigational therapy, in development for phlebotomy-dependent polycythemia vera (PV) ─ to Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany’s pipeline. Divesiran is dosed subcutaneously once every 3 months.
PV is a chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm ─ a type of rare blood cancer ─ characterized by the excessive production of red blood cells, which can be associated with a higher rate of death from cardiovascular and thrombotic events.
Divesiran is designed to selectively silence TMPRSS6, a gene involved in regulating hepcidin, the body’s key regulator of iron metabolism. By increasing hepcidin levels, Divesiran aims to limit iron availability for red blood cell production, helping to control hematocrit levels and potentially reducing the need for frequent therapeutic phlebotomies.
Divesiran met its primary endpoint in the Phase 2 SANRECO study with an 88% responder rate versus 19% for placebo (p “The planned acquisition of Silence Therapeutics marks a significant step forward in our strategy to become a Global Specialty Innovator in Healthcare,” said Danny Bar-Zohar, member of the Executive Board and CEO Healthcare at Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany. “Silence Therapeutics’ primary siRNA pipeline asset, Divesiran, is supported by promising Phase 2 efficacy data, a potentially best-in-class, once-every-three-month dosing schedule, and a safety profile that appears manageable, with the added advantage of targeting a well-defined, homogeneous patient population. The planned acquisition also provides an entry point into hematology through a biologically validated mechanism of action. With this transaction, we are advancing our efforts to build a differentiated, sustainable pipeline as we bring more medicines to more patients, faster.”
“We are pleased to have reached this agreement with Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, which follows a competitive sale process and delivers significant, immediate and certain value to our shareholders,” said Iain Ross, Interim Principal Executive Officer and Chairman of the Silence Therapeutics’ Board. “This transaction follows potentially best-in-class Phase 2 polycythemia vera data for Divesiran and reflects the important progress we have made advancing our differentiated siRNA pipeline. It also provides a new home for our innovative programs within Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, placing Divesiran with a company that has the scale, resources and commercial capabilities to accelerate its Phase 3 development and bring this potentially best-in-class siRNA therapy to patients in need. We are incredibly grateful to our employees for their dedication and contributions in building Silence Therapeutics into the company it is today.”
The transaction has been unanimously approved by Silence Therapeutics’ Board of Directors and Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany’s relevant corporate bodies and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to satisfaction of customary closing conditions, including receipt of required regulatory approvals and approval by Silence Therapeutics’ shareholders. In connection with the transaction, certain securityholders of Silence Therapeutics holding securities representing approximately 14% of Silence Therapeutics’ voting power have entered into a voting and support agreement with Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, under which the securityholders have agreed among other things, to vote their voting securities of Silence Therapeutics in favor of the transaction. Silence Therapeutics is a UK company, with ADSs, each representing three of its ordinary shares, listed on NASDAQ. As is customary for similar transactions, the transaction will be effected through a UK scheme of arrangement.
The planned acquisition will be funded through proceeds from new debt.
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany is committed to leveraging advanced technologies and data science to accelerate the discovery and delivery of breakthrough medicines. This acquisition is another step forward in its broader strategy to enhance research productivity and the output of its pipeline sustainably, focusing on indications that can be derisked through proper preclinical and early clinical testing to ensure that more patients gain access to effective treatments.
Silence Therapeutics employs approximately 80 people and operates from locations in the UK, the US and Germany.
A&O Shearman is acting as legal counsel to Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany.

FAIRINO and Schmalz Sign Global Ecosystem Strategic Partnership Agreement
Edited by Yara From Gasgoo | October 17 , 2026 14:58 BJT 
f SHARE TWEET in SHARE SHARE 
Scan for mobile
Gasgoo Munich- FAIRINO and German vacuum automation specialist Schmalz officially signed a global strategic partnership agreement at the Schmalz booth during the Shanghai Industrial Fair On Oct. 14. The two parties will deepen cooperation across multiple dimensions, including product adaptation, standardized solutions, and global market coordination.
Image Source: FAIRINO
Under the agreement, both sides will leverage their respective strengths in global service networks and product technology. They plan to focus on typical industrial scenarios such as palletizing and CNC machine tending to jointly drive the development and global rollout of automation solutions.
Schmalz has already completed technical adaptation of its robotic gripper series for FAIRINO's full lineup of collaborative robots and launched a dedicated handling kit for FAIRINO, laying the groundwork for the joint promotion of standardized solutions. By combining collaborative robots with end-of-arm tooling, the partners aim to further streamline product selection and application deployment.
On the market front, the two companies have already established a solid foundation in Europe, North America, and South Korea. Schmalz's gripping products and FAIRINO's collaborative robots are gradually generating synergies in the application and promotion efforts across these regions.
Teams in Europe, the U.S., South Korea, and Vietnam are maintaining close communication, coordinating product recommendations and solution collaboration based on actual customer needs. Following this signing, the companies plan to further expand into the Chinese and Southeast Asian markets, working together to build a broader global ecosystem.
Public records show that Schmalz was founded in 1910 and has long specialized in vacuum automation and ergonomic handling systems. Its product portfolio covers vacuum components, gripping systems, and automated handling solutions, with business extending across multiple global markets.
FAIRINO, meanwhile, focuses on the R&D and manufacturing of collaborative robots. Leveraging proprietary intellectual property and localized service networks, it is advancing its international layout. The company aims to lead global sales in the industry by 2025, with overseas shipments projected to approach 6,000 units in 2026.
This signing marks an upgrade from product-level adaptation to a long-term ecosystem synergy. Looking ahead, the two will launch joint marketing campaigns centered on standardized product combinations. By integrating robot bodies, gripping technology, and global market resources, they aim to refine their cooperation system and drive large-scale deployment of products and solutions across more industrial scenarios.

Cell therapy weekly: stem cell therapy for osteoarthritis
15 Oct 2026 
Written by Megan Giboney 
Cancer

The week in cell therapy 
This week: a new manufacturing facility for Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) grade small molecules opened in Bristol, UK, a collaboration leveraging cGMP Next-Generation Sequencing-based viral safety testing to advance a stem cell therapy for osteoarthritis was announced, and a pre-clinical CAR-T portfolio was sold for €8 million.
The news highlights:
New UK facility boosts GMP small molecule manufacturing for cell therapies 
Collaboration to advance stem cell therapy for osteoarthritis 
Early-stage CAR-T portfolio sold for €8 million 
New UK facility boosts GMP small molecule manufacturing for cell therapies
Bio-Techne Corporation (MN, USA) has announced the opening of its new purpose-built 10,000-square-foot GMP manufacturing facility in Bristol, UK, strengthening the company’s global GMP manufacturing infrastructure.
The facility has five ISO-8 multifunctional cleanrooms and two ISO-7 cleanrooms dedicated to small molecule manufacturing and product handling.
“As the cell therapy field continues to mature, success increasingly depends on the ability to manufacture therapies consistently and at scale,” said Kim Kelderman, President and Chief Executive Officer of Bio-Techne. “Our investment in Bristol demonstrates Bio-Techne’s commitment to providing customers with the GMP materials, manufacturing expertise, and supply chain reliability needed to accelerate development and ultimately bring transformative therapies to patients worldwide.”
Read more 
Collaboration to advance stem cell therapy for osteoarthritis
Charles River Laboratories (MA, USA) and Magellan Stem Cells (Victoria, Australia) have announced a partnership to advance the development and commercialization of Magellan’s lead proprietary allogeneic, off-the-shelf stem cell therapy candidate (Zelestrocel) for osteoarthritis.
Magellan has recently completed Phase I/II trials for Zelestrocel and is now moving toward a Phase III study. The company has also built manufacturing capacity directly into its development process, having obtained GMP certification from Australia’s Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) for its production site in Melbourne.
Under the agreement, Charles River will provide cGMP Next-Generation Sequencing-based viral safety testing for Zelestrocel to support regulatory readiness.
“As we prepare for the next stage of Zelestrocel’s development, having access to advanced testing technologies and collaborating with experienced partners is critical to our success,” said Magellan Stem Cells CEO Julien Freitag.
Read more 
Early-stage CAR-T portfolio sold for €8 million
Lakefront Biotherapeutics (formerly Galapagos NV; Mechelen, Belgium) has announced the completed sale of its early-stage cell therapy portfolio to Armed Cell Therapeutics (Brussels, Belgium). Under the deal terms, Lakefront will receive €8 million upfront, with the possibility of earning up to $230 million in future milestone payments plus a modest royalty on sales.
The divested assets include a range of multi-targeting and armed CAR-T constructs engineered to enhance the potency and persistence of CAR-T therapies while addressing treatment resistance in hematological cancers and solid tumors.
“I’m pleased we were able to complete this sale of the early-stage cell therapy programs as it provides a path to continue to advance these assets on behalf of patients. Additionally, it offers Lakefront shareholders the opportunity to benefit from their potential future progress by the experienced team at Armed Cell Therapeutics,” said Sooin Kwon, Chief Business Officer of Lakefront. “Lakefront continues to be in an enviable position with a rich legacy of innovation, an exciting newly established pipeline of T-cell engagers and a strong cash balance.”

Prodrive Technologies participates in SEMICON West 2026, held at the Moscone Center in San Francisco from Oct. 13 to 15. (Photo: THE ELEC) 
Dutch company Prodrive Technologies plans to open an office in South Korea between late 2026 and early 2027 to strengthen support for local customers, including Hanwha Semitech, and expand its presence through sales activities.
At SEMICON West 2026, held at the Moscone Center in San Francisco on Oct. 13, Prodrive said it was recruiting local employees in preparation for the office opening. “We expect to open around the end of this year or early next year,” the company said. It is considering Dongtan and Pangyo as potential locations.
The Korean office will handle sales and customer support, with a small team being recruited. Prodrive is also building a new manufacturing facility in Malaysia. It operates production sites in the Netherlands, Boston in the US, and China, as well as sales offices in Japan and Israel. The company employs approximately 2,300 people worldwide.
Prodrive develops modules and provides system integration services for semiconductor equipment manufacturers. Rather than selling finished equipment directly to chipmakers, it designs and integrates equipment modules to meet manufacturers’ requirements. Its core products include precision stages, motion controllers, motors, actuators and high-speed cameras used in applications requiring high-precision control. It also produces equipment for front-end metrology and inspection and back-end hybrid bonding.
In South Korea, Hanwha Semitech collaborated with Prodrive to develop a hybrid bonder. Earlier this year, the second-generation hybrid bonder, SHB2 Nano, was manufactured and assembled at Prodrive’s Netherlands facility before being brought to South Korea. Prodrive also supplies linear motors and servo drives for magnetic levitation systems used in ASML’s extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography equipment.
“The Korean office will be responsible for sales and customer support,” a Prodrive representative said. “We have no plans to establish manufacturing facilities in Korea because we can support Korean customers from Malaysia, China and Europe.”

Vestas has announced new wind turbine orders totalling approximately 92 MW across three onshore wind projects in Germany, in collaboration with BBWind Projektberatungsgesellschaft mbH. The orders, included in the company’s third-quarter (Q3) order intake, cover the supply of 13 wind turbines and include 20-year Active Output Management (AOM) 5000 service agreements.
The projects, located in Borken and Raesfeld, will feature Vestas’ V172-7.2 MW and V162-5.6 MW turbine models, supporting the continued expansion of Germany’s onshore wind energy capacity.
The first order covers the 42 MW Borken Kierit wind project, developed by Windenergie Kierit GmbH & Co. KG in association with BBWind Projektberatungsgesellschaft mbH. Vestas will supply five V172-7.2 MW turbines and one V162-5.6 MW turbine for the project. Deliveries are scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2027, with commissioning expected to commence in the second quarter of 2028. The agreement includes a 20-year AOM 5000 service contract to support long-term turbine performance and operational reliability.
The second agreement involves the 29 MW Raesfeld Lanzenhagen wind project, developed by Windenergie Lanzenhagen GmbH & Co. KG in collaboration with BBWind. The project will feature four V172-7.2 MW wind turbines, with deliveries planned to begin in the first quarter of 2028 and commissioning scheduled to commence in the fourth quarter of 2028. The contract also includes a 20-year AOM 5000 service agreement.
The third order covers the 22 MW Borken Deepschlatt wind project, developed by Windenergie Deepschlatt GmbH & Co. KG alongside BBWind. Vestas will deliver three V172-7.2 MW wind turbines, with deliveries expected to begin in the first quarter of 2028 and commissioning scheduled to start in the third quarter of 2028. The project will also benefit from a 20-year AOM 5000 service agreement.
Also Read   Agrivoltaics World Conference 2026 Highlights India’s Push To Combine Food Production, Solar Power And Higher Farmer Incomes 
Across the three projects, Vestas will supply 12 V172-7.2 MW turbines and one V162-5.6 MW turbine, representing a combined turbine capacity of approximately 92 MW. The long-term service agreements are designed to support operational efficiency, turbine availability, and reliable electricity generation throughout the projects’ operating lives.
The latest orders highlight continued investment in Germany’s onshore wind sector and reinforce Vestas’ collaboration with BBWind in developing renewable energy infrastructure.
The projects are expected to contribute to Germany’s renewable energy expansion by increasing wind power generation capacity, strengthening domestic clean electricity supply, and supporting the country’s broader energy transition and decarbonisation objectives.

title: Applied Materials opens $5B semiconductor innovation center - Manufacturing Dive
content_text:
Applied Materials opens $5B semiconductor innovation center
The EPIC Center is the world’s largest semiconductor equipment and process technology research and development facility, the company said.
Published Oct. 15, 2026
Jeff Kinney

A render of Applied Materials' new Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization Center. The company announced the center, where capital investment is expected to reach $5 billion, at its Sunnyvale, California, campus on Oct. 12.
Courtesy of Applied Materials
Listen to the article
3 min 
This audio is auto-generated. Please let us know if you have feedback .
Dive Brief:
Applied Materials , an equipment, services and software supplier for chipmakers, has opened its multibillion-dollar Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization Center to collaborate with industry on next-generation technologies.
Leading chipmakers, systems companies, equipment partners and research universities will work at the center to develop advanced chipmaking processes, as well as to move technologies from early-stage research to high-volume manufacturing faster, Applied Materials said.
The 600,000-square-foot facility is located at the company’s campus in Sunnyvale, California, and has near four acres of advanced cleanroom space. Applied Materials said it expects capital spending to reach $5 billion as new customer projects begin.
Dive Insight:
The news comes several months after Applied Materials announced it had partnered with South Korea-based SK Hynix to accelerate memory innovation and address semiconductor-related challenges at the EPIC Center. The agreement was reached as technology firms navigate a global shortage of memory chips driven by surging artificial intelligence demand.
According to Applied Materials, the EPIC Center will “reinvent” the standard research and development model in the semiconductor industry. The standard model typically involves handing off foundational materials research, equipment and process development, and process integration and pilot produciton from one siloed environment to the next.
“The EPIC Center is designed to remove these handoffs, putting the people who invent the materials, build the equipment, and make the chips together in a state-of-the-art facility purpose-built for commercialization,” the company said. “The technologies the AI era demands are too complex and too consequential for any one company to invent alone.”
Applied Materials said it expects the center’s operating model to provide chipmakers early access to advanced materials and equipment, shorter learning cycles and a faster path to volume production. 
Materials innovation has “outgrown serial development” and “demands coordinated development and integrated solutions,” Prabu Raja, president of Applied Materials’ semiconductor products group, said in a statement. “EPIC is the only place where materials, process technology and equipment will be innovated in parallel, which increases the success rate of new materials and technologies.”
Partners in the EPIC Center “span the AI technology stack” and include TSMC, Intel, SK Hynix, Micron, Samsung Electronics, Broadcom and Advantest, along with Arizona State University, Stanford University, University of California, Berkeley and other institutions. More companies and organizations are expected to join the center over time.
Applied Materials reported $7.01 billion in Q1 revenue , above the midpoint of its guided range, citing increased demand for leading-edge logic, high-bandwidth memory and advanced packaging.

title: Tosoh Takes Full Control of HDI Monomer Producer Nanyo Kasei - ChemAnalyst
query: ("Tosoh" OR "Tosoh Corporation") ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Tosoh Takes Full Control of HDI Monomer Producer Nanyo Kasei
George Orwell 15-Oct-2026 
Tosoh will acquire Asahi Kasei's 50% stake in Nanyo Kasei, securing full ownership and strengthening HDI monomer supply for derivatives production.
Tosoh Corporation has moved to strengthen its control over the supply chain for hexamethylene diisocyanate (HDI) monomer by acquiring the remaining 50% stake in Nanyo Kasei Co., Ltd. from Asahi Kasei Corporation. The transaction will transform the existing joint venture into a wholly owned subsidiary of Tosoh, supporting the company's efforts to secure raw material supplies and strengthen its downstream HDI derivatives business. 
Established in 1980, Nanyo Kasei was formed through equal investments by Nippon Polyurethane Industry Co., Ltd., now part of Tosoh Corporation, and Asahi Kasei Corporation. The joint venture was established specifically to manufacture HDI monomer, an important chemical intermediate used in the production of HDI-based derivatives. 
Under the existing arrangement, Tosoh and Asahi Kasei supply raw materials and other inputs to Nanyo Kasei. The company manufactures HDI monomer, which is subsequently purchased by both shareholders for their respective manufacturing operations. Following the acquisition, Tosoh will gain full ownership of the production facility and greater control over its operations and output allocation. 
The strategic move is primarily aimed at ensuring a stable supply of HDI monomer, a critical feedstock for Tosoh's downstream derivatives business. By bringing Nanyo Kasei entirely under its ownership, Tosoh expects to strengthen supply-chain coordination, improve procurement certainty and support the consistent operation of its HDI derivatives manufacturing activities. 
The acquisition is particularly significant because Tosoh's new HDI derivatives plant commenced commercial operations in September 2026. Securing reliable access to HDI monomer will be important for maintaining production continuity at the new facility and supporting the company's downstream business requirements. Full ownership of Nanyo Kasei is expected to give Tosoh greater flexibility in aligning monomer production with the demand generated by its derivatives operations. 
HDI is widely used to manufacture aliphatic polyisocyanates, which serve as curing agents in polyurethane coatings. These products are valued for their weather resistance, durability, colour stability and long-term performance. They are used in automotive refinishing, industrial coatings, protective finishes and other applications requiring high-performance surface protection. 
Although the acquisition strengthens Tosoh's control over an important upstream asset, its immediate effect on the wider HDI market will depend on production volumes, operating rates, demand conditions and the availability of competing supplies. The announcement does not specify any additional production capacity or a planned increase in HDI monomer output. 
Overall, the transaction represents a strategic vertical-integration move, positioning Tosoh to better coordinate HDI monomer procurement with its expanding derivatives operations while reinforcing supply reliability for its downstream customers. 
Product and Chemical Price Impact 
Tosoh's acquisition is expected to improve HDI monomer supply security for its downstream derivatives business, particularly following the September 2026 startup of its new derivatives plant. However, the deal does not confirm additional production capacity or increased market supply, limiting the likelihood of an immediate price impact. Greater operational integration could improve procurement efficiency and reduce supply disruptions for Tosoh. HDI monomer and HDI-based polyisocyanate prices may remain influenced by feedstock costs, plant operating rates, demand from automotive and industrial coatings, and competing suppliers. Any broader price softening would depend on increased output rather than ownership changes alone.

What We Thought of ASML Holding’s Earnings
Last quarter, ASML Holding ASML announced plans to expand low-NA EUV and immersion DUV capacity by 30% in 2027 and another 30% in 2028. These plans seem already outdated, as management has acknowledged this might not be enough to meet customer demand.
Why it matters: ASML’s backlog keeps growing, with 2027 fully booked and significant order intake already for 2028. In our view, the most important disclosure from these earnings was that ASML is having first conversations with customers for 2029 and 2030 orders. DRAM makers seem the most open to talking about 2029-30 already.
While we still see some upside to our 2028 revenue and EPS forecast as ASML tries to expand capacity beyond 30% with its existing footprint, we believe most of it is already priced in. What could push the stock higher is order visibility that confirms 2029 and 2030 as “growth years.”
The bottom line: We maintain our wide Morningstar Economic Moat Rating and EUR 1,800 fair value estimate.
After 28% sales growth in both 2027 and 2028, reaching EUR 56 and EUR 71.5 billion respectively, we model a return to low-double-digit growth in 2029 and 2030, with sales reaching EUR 88 billion in 2030. Should management confirm the first 2029 orders over the next six months, our 2029-30 forecast would gain credibility, and the stock price could converge toward our fair value estimate.
Our bull case would require 2029 to book as quickly and as fully as 2028 has. If customers place orders at a fast pace in the coming months, sales growth in 2029-30 could exceed our low-double-digit forecast.
Key stats: Beyond expanding capacity, ASML continues to aggressively develop upgrades to low-NA EUV and immersion DUV output. Installed base management revenue reached EUR 3.3 billion, EUR 400 million higher than expected, thanks to the upgrade business, as customers look to extract more productivity from their machines. Upgrades were the main driver of the 57.5% gross margin this quarter, above guidance of 55.0%-57.0%.

title: The Maxon Fall 2026 Release Delivers Bigger Worlds, Faster Workflows, and More Creative Control - USA Today
