content_text:
The Maxon Fall 2026 Release Delivers Bigger Worlds, Faster Workflows, and More Creative Control
Maxon Computers
New Cinema 4D Scatter and Liquid FX, integrated UV workflows in ZBrush, faster Redshift interaction, art-directable VFX in Red Giant, and MCP-powered Autograph workflows give artists more capability, speed and control. 
BAD HOMBURG, GERMANY / ACCESS Newswire / October 14, 2026 / Maxon , maker of powerful, approachable software solutions for creators working in 2D and 3D design, motion graphics, visual effects and visualization, today announced its Fall 2026 ecosystem release , which introduces the 2027.0 releases of Cinema 4D, ZBrush, Redshift, Red Giant and Autograph, bringing substantial new creative capabilities and workflow improvements across the Maxon toolset. In the 2027.0 release, Maxon is delivering new ways to populate and simulate complex 3D worlds, more complete production workflows inside ZBrush, faster rendering feedback in Redshift, new art-directable VFX capabilities, and deeper creative automation and cross-application workflows in Autograph through Model Context Protocol (MCP) support and first direct connection with Cinema 4D.
“We’re continuing to do what we’ve always done: listen to our artists and bring the best tools we can to them,” said David McGavran, CEO of Maxon. “Everything we build adds to what came before it, so the possibilities keep getting bigger. A few years ago, you couldn’t simulate a beer in Cinema 4D. Now you can pour it, foam it, spray it and make it look almost as satisfying as the real thing. That’s the kind of progress we want artists to feel: faster workflows, fewer barriers and more of the real world available to create.”
Build Bigger, Richer Worlds in Cinema 4D 
Cinema 4D 2027.0 delivers an all new Scatter System , one of the product’s most requested capabilities, giving artists a procedural way to populate environments with vegetation, rocks, debris, crowds and other objects while maintaining precise creative control.
The new Scatter Generator and Scatter Tag support distribution, filtering, clustering and transform controls, while integration with Cinema 4D’s MoGraph toolset lets artists use familiar Fields and Effectors to shape, animate and influence scattered objects. The updates give artists a more approachable path to building dense, believable environments without relying on complex workarounds or separate scattering tools.
Cinema 4D’s unified simulation system now also includes Liquid FX , adding automatically generated foam, spray and bubbles to liquid simulations. These secondary effects respond to the underlying liquid behavior, adding the visual detail that makes pours, splashes, waterfalls and other fluid effects feel more convincing without requiring artists to construct separate complex simulations.
The release also deepens the connection between Cinema 4D and Redshift – including ACES 2.0 alignment improvements – streamlines everyday workflows, and introduces a range of quality-of-life upgrades designed to make routine production work faster and less prone to error.
An End-to-End Sculpting Pipeline in ZBrush, from iPad to Desktop 
Artists have been asking for ways to do more of their production workflow without needing to leave the ZBrush environment – and now they can.
A new UV Editor lets artists create, edit and refine UVs directly inside ZBrush, with professional workflow support including UDIMs and texel density controls. Built using proven Maxon technology from Cinema 4D, the editor reduces the back-and-forth between applications while artists are still iterating on a sculpt, helping them move more quickly from sculpting and painting into texturing and downstream production.
New Selection Sets tackle another everyday pain point by allowing artists to save and recall Polygroups, masks, Polypaint, morph targets and UV configurations rather than repeatedly rebuilding them by hand. For complex iterative work, that means less time recreating selections and more freedom to explore different ideas.
ZBrush for iPad continues to become a more complete professional sculpting environment with Spotlight, bringing reference, projection, painting and image-driven sculpting workflows to iPad. New non-destructive 3D Layers enable artists to experiment freely on the iPad with sculpting, polypaint and masking on a layer, giving more control over sculpting changes, detail blending, and creative iteration.
Rendering in Redshift Means Less Time Waiting, More Time Creating 
Cinema 4D and Redshift 2027.0 give artists speed where it matters most: while the creativity is flowing.
A reworked memory architecture uses available memory more efficiently across an increasingly wide range of hardware, while major interactivity improvements shorten the time between making a change and seeing the rendered result. For artists, that means less lag time between an idea and the visual feedback needed to refine it. Change a light, material or scene element and understand its impact on the environment more quickly for a more fluid creative experience.
Redshift also continues to feel more native inside Cinema 4D. Artists can more easily drag Cinema 4D objects, Cloners and particle systems directly into material workflows and access their properties in the Node Editor, simplifying tasks that previously required more steps. Creative flexibility is further enhanced through a new procedural system for generating fur, fibers, textiles, and knitted materials directly at render time, while support for NVIDIA RTX Spark brings Redshift workflows to a wider range of power-efficient mobile devices and production environments.
Red Giant Introduces Art-Directable Visual Effects 
Red Giant 2027.0 brings powerful updates to VFX artists, motion designers, and content creators, making visual effects faster, more intuitive, and more art-directable across creative workflows.
Scene Light , a new AI-powered, depth-aware relighting tool, lets artists place lights into existing live-action footage and CG imagery directly in After Effects. Artists can add realistic interactive light from effects such as muzzle flashes, explosions, and environmental sources, or make broader changes such as day-for-night treatments, without relying on extensive masking and manual color adjustments. Lights remain fully art-directable within the compositing workflow.
Maxon Noise for Universe brings the procedural noise patterns familiar to Cinema 4D and Redshift into video and compositing workflows. Long requested by the community, Maxon Noise gives motion designers and VFX artists GPU-accelerated tools for building textures, animated maps, transitions and abstract effects directly within their existing workflows.
Real Lens Flares becomes more flexible and physically grounded with Custom Schmutz, which lets artists use their own still or animated textures for lens grime, splashes and imperfections, alongside expanded Light Source Types for creating flares appropriate to different real-world lighting sources rather than treating every source like sunlight.
Chromatic Displacement also comes to Autograph, extending the Red Giant toolset available inside Maxon’s free motion graphics and compositing application, while new Custom UI support in Maxon Studio allows Capsules to expose richer Red Giant controls including color wheels, curves, gradients and text controls.
New Autograph MCP Server Gives Artists a Productivity Boost 
Autograph 2027.0 now supports an MCP Server that can be switched on to bridge AI agents to Autograph’s own tools, helping artists navigate the software and increase creative output.
The new MCP Server opens Autograph to agentic AI workflows, allowing supported AI tools to assist with tasks inside the application, answer questions about how to use Autograph, or automate portions of a creative workflow, all through natural language prompting. The integration is designed to work with Autograph’s native tools and workflows, giving artists the ability to continue editing and directing the work inside the application.
Autograph also now has its first direct connection with Cinema 4D: artists can copy and paste 3D elements directly from Cinema 4D into Autograph, including animated elements, cameras, lights, nulls and compatible primitives. This brings the applications closer together as a unified 3D and compositing workflow, letting artists combine Cinema 4D scenes and Redshift renders with Autograph’s native 3D workspace without rebuilding key scene information by hand.
Listen. Build. Deliver. 
The Maxon 2027.0 release continues a year of development across Maxon’s tools. Throughout 2026, Maxon has shipped new capabilities, platform support, performance improvements and workflow refinements as they became ready rather than asking artists to wait for one annual product drop.
“We’re focused on giving artists more of what they need to create, removing friction from the parts of the process that slow them down, and improving the technology underneath the tools they use every day,” said McGavran.
Availability 
The new releases of Cinema 4D, ZBrush, Redshift, Red Giant and Autograph will be available beginning October 14, 2026.
About Maxon 
Maxon makes powerful, yet approachable software solutions for content creators working in 2D and 3D design, motion graphics, visual effects and visualization. Product lines include the award-winning Cinema 4D suite of 3D modeling, simulation and animation technology; the diverse Red Giant lineup of editing, motion design and filmmaking tools; the leading-edge Redshift renderer; ZBrush, the industry-standard digital sculpting and painting solution; and Autograph, Maxon’s motion graphics and compositing application.

Tosoh to acquire Asahi Kasei’s stake in HDI monomer JV, taking full ownership
October 14, 2026 | By Mary Bailey 
Tosoh Corp. (Tokyo) has decided to acquire all shares (50%) of Nanyo Kasei Co., Ltd. (Tokyo), a joint venture with Asahi Kasei Corp. (Tokyo). The deal will make Nanyo Kasei a wholly owned subsidiary of Tosoh.
Nanyo Kasei was established in 1980 through equal investment by Nippon Polyurethane Industry Co., Ltd. (now Tosoh) and Asahi Kasei to manufacture hexamethylene diisocyanate (HDI) monomer .
Currently, Tosoh and Asahi Kasei supply raw materials and other inputs to Nanyo Kasei, which manufactures the HDI monomer. Each company then purchases the monomer for its own operations. Tosoh will acquire the 50% of Nanyo Kasei shares held by Asahi Kasei.
Through the full acquisition, Tosoh aims to secure a stable supply of HDI monomer and support the stable operation of its HDI derivatives business. The transaction will also contribute to the stable procurement of HDI monomer for Tosoh’s new HDI derivatives plant, which began commercial operations in September 2026.
Tosoh expects the impact of the transaction on its consolidated financial results for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027, to be minimal.

Charles River partners with Magellan Stem Cells on cell therapy
The partnership focuses on biologics quality control as well as viral and release testing under cGMP standards.
Salong Debbarma

Charles River will supply viral safety assessments using NGS for cell and gene therapy. Credit: Gorodenkoff/Shutterstock.com. 
Charles River Laboratories International (CRL) has collaborated with Australian biotechnology firm Magellan Stem Cells to advance the development and clinical progress of Magellan’s regenerative medicine candidate, Zelestrocel.
The partnership focuses on biologics quality control as well as viral and release testing under current good manufacturing practice (cGMP) standards.

Magellan recently completed Phase I/II clinical studies evaluating Zelestrocel, an off-the-shelf, allogeneic stem cell therapy designed to treat osteoarthritis.
The company is now preparing to initiate a pivotal Phase III clinical programme.
Charles River global manufacturing corporate senior vice president Kerstin Dolph said: “Working with organisations at the forefront of innovation allows us to expand our GMP testing capabilities and help accelerate the delivery of safe, compliant therapies to patients.
“We are excited to support Magellan as they work towards advancing Zelestrocel from the clinic to potential commercialisation.”
To support the therapy’s progress towards international regulatory standards, Charles River will provide viral safety assessments using next-generation sequencing (NGS) for cell and gene therapy (CGT).
The testing protocols comply with regulatory benchmarks from the European Medicines Agency (EMA), the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), GMP standards, and International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) Q5A and Q5B guidelines.
Charles River expanded its sequencing capabilities through the acquisition of Pathoquest, a company specialising in biopharmaceutical quality control and characterisation.
Magellan COO Nick Bliesner said: “Charles River’s GMP NGS capabilities provide an innovative approach to viral safety testing that supports both product quality and regulatory readiness. This collaboration strengthens our ability to advance Zelestrocel toward commercialisation with confidence.”
Magellan manufactures the cell therapy internally at its Melbourne facility, which holds GMP certification from the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA).
It is one of only four cell therapy manufacturing centres in Australia to hold GMP certification.
The sequencing work also aligns with Charles River’s Alternative Methods Advancement Project (AMAP), an initiative guided by a scientific advisory board chaired by Dr Namandjé Bumpus to reduce animal testing by implementing new approach methodologies (NAMs).
In addition, Charles River operates nine CGMP-compliant International Organization for Standardization-6 (ISO-6) cleanroom suites, offers cell bank release within eight to ten weeks, and has produced more than 2,000 cell and viral banks.
In August this year, CRL and Medigen Vaccine Biologics (MVC) entered into a collaboration to support the characterisation and validation of the virus seed bank for MVC’s next-generation multivalent enterovirus vaccine.

content_text:
Tosoh to take full control of PU monomer producer
14 Oct 2026
Share: 
Acquisition from Asahi Kasei to support supply to newly commissioned HDI derivatives plant
Tokyo – Tosoh Corp. is to acquire Asahi Kasei's 50% interest in Nanyo Kasei, taking full ownership of the Japanese producer of hexamethylene diisocyanate (HDI) monomer.
Nanyo Kasei was established in 1980 as a 50:50 joint venture between Asahi Kasei and Nippon Polyurethane Industry, now part of Tosoh, to manufacture HDI monomer.
Under the current arrangement, Tosoh and Asahi Kasei supply raw materials and other inputs to Nanyo Kasei and subsequently purchase the HDI monomer produced by the company.
In a 13 Oct statement, Tosoh said the acquisition would enable it to “secure a stable supply of HDI monomer” and support the stable operation of its HDI derivatives business.
In particular, the group said the transaction would support HDI monomer supply to its new HDI derivatives plant, which started commercial operations in September.
The acquisition is scheduled to close by the end of March 2027.

content_text:
ASML says it's getting order interest through 2030 as profit smashes expectations
Published Wed, Oct 14 2026 1:14 AM EDT Updated Wed, Oct 14 2026 4:45 AM EDT 
Arjun Kharpal @/in/arjunkharpal/ @ArjunKharpal 
WATCH LIVE 
Key Points
ASML said some customers are "expressing an interest" in placing orders with the company in 2029 and 2030, providing investors with a view into longer-term demand.
The Dutch chip giant said it is looking at ways to increase capacity for 2028 beyond the 30% increase it had previously forecast as demand remains strong.
The company also raised the lower end of its sales forecast for 2026.
In this article
ASML 
TSM 
Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT 
ASML said Wednesday that some of its customers are expressing interest in placing orders for its critical semiconductor tools for 2029 and 2030 as the company reported third-quarter profit that beat expectations.
The comments will likely comfort investors who have been looking to assess the longer-term demand outlook for ASML's lithography machines.
"Our customers continue to increase their short- and medium-term equipment demand forecasts with us, driven primarily by their views on the size and duration of AI-related investments," CEO Christophe Fouquet said in a press release. 
"In light of their demand visibility, some customers are expressing an interest in placing orders with us for 2029 and even 2030."
ASML is the only company in the world that produces extreme ultraviolet lithography machines, a key tool used by the likes of TSMC to make the world's most advanced semiconductors. 
Investors closely watch the Dutch company's earnings for signs of AI-related chip demand. 
watch now 
VIDEO 3:47 03:47 
ASML races to expand capacity on strong AI-driven demand
Squawk Box Europe 
Fouquet said current supply planned for 2027 and 2028 will not fully meet the demand of its customers. The company is "investigating ways" to increase capacity for 2028 beyond the 30% increase it had previously forecast. 
ASML has now updated its guidance three times this year, upping its full-year forecast for the second time in July, and on Wednesday it raised the lower end of its sales forecast for 2026. 
The company now expects net sales of between 44 billion euros and 45 billion euros ($49.3 billion to $50.4 billion). The previous lower end of the forecast was for 43 billion euros.
ASML also said it expects fourth-quarter net sales of between 14.2 billion euros and 15.2 billion euros. The upper end of the range is ahead of LSEG consensus estimates of 14.2 billion euros. 
ASML's stock was around 2% higher in early trade in Europe. Shares of the company have rallied 56% this year. 
ASML shares year-to-date
During the quarter, Samsung and TSMC, the world's two biggest chipmakers, committed to using ASML's High NA extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines. High NA EUV is ASML's next-generation tool, which analysts see as key to the Dutch firm's future growth.
For the third quarter, here's how ASML did versus LSEG consensus estimates:
Net sales: 11.66 billion euros versus 11.72 billion euros expected
Net profit: 4.96 billion euros versus 4.1 billion euros expected 
ASML sticks to China forecast 
The semiconductor equipment maker said it expects China sales to account for 20% of its total business, sticking to a prior forecast.
While ASML holds an effective monopoly on EUV machines, a July report from The Information suggested an unnamed Chinese company had begun manufacturing an immersion deep ultraviolet lithography (DUV) machine, citing people familiar with the matter.
ASML dominates the manufacturing of DUV machines, which are less advanced than EUV. China has been ramping up its domestic semiconductor supply chain, with some investors concerned it could challenge the European and U.S. dominance. However, analysts raised questions about China's ability to ramp up its own DUV technology. 
ASML meanwhile has faced challenges in China over the last few years. The company is restricted from selling EUV and some DUV tools to China.

Strong operational performance at Oyu Tolgoi copper and Pilbara iron ore 
MELBOURNE, Australia, October 13, 2026 --( BUSINESS WIRE )--Rio Tinto Chief Executive Simon Trott said: "We delivered strong operational performance in the third quarter. Oyu Tolgoi copper production increased 29% year-to-date, with the operation running at a ~450 kt annualised rate in the quarter, and global iron ore sales are up 3% year-to-date. The Simandou iron ore mine hit an annualised production run-rate of ~10 Mtpa (100% basis) in the quarter as the project continues to ramp up. 
"We are finishing the year with momentum, with significant opportunities to accelerate improvements in safety, productivity and reliability through implementation of our operating system. We remain on track for a $1.8 billion annualised productivity benefit run-rate by the end of 2026. Our major projects remain on schedule and budget, underwriting our growth profile to 2030. 
"We made further significant steps in decarbonising our business in the third quarter, with our Pacific Aluminium smelter repowering arrangements now well progressed. 
"Today, we announce that we have achieved more than $2 billion1 of capital release year-to-date, as we actively manage our portfolio with discipline to maximise long-term value, as part of the $5 to 10 billion capital release program."

Operational excellence: ~1% YTD increase in copper equivalent (CuEq2) production, driven by growth from Oyu Tolgoi copper and Pilbara iron ore.

Iron ore: Q3 global iron ore sales were 90.8 Mt, up 3% YoY, while Pilbara sales increased 2% YoY. Simandou hit an annualised production run-rate of ~10 Mtpa (100% basis) in Q3 as the project ramps up and remains on track to reach a 60 Mtpa production run-rate during H2 20283. 
Aluminium : Consistent, stable performance across the full operating system. Pacific smelter repowering arrangements are now well progressed, following the Tomago and Bell Bay power agreements in Q3.

content_text:
AVL and VisIC reveal GaN-based EV traction inverter
Tuesday 13th October 2026
Demonstrator vehicle uses D³GaN power modules in an advanced electric drivetrain 
VisIC, a developer of high-power GaN chips, and AVL, a mobility technology company, have worked together on integrating VisIC's D³GaN power module technology into AVL's vehicle demonstrator.
The demonstrator combines a high-speed e-axle, advanced power electronics and vehicle control technologies, with a GaN traction inverter using VisIC power modules. The overall project brings together technology from AVL, NXP Semiconductors and VisIC Technologies. 
It builds on a two year collaboration between AVL and VisIC. In earlier Dyno WLTC testing at AVL facilities in Germany, an inverter based on VisIC's GaN-on-Silicon D³GaN technology is claimed to have achieved 99.67 percent efficiency at 10 kHz and more than 99.8 percent at 5 kHz on AVL's e-motor test bench. The companies reported an improvement compared with comparable SiC inverters and a reduction of inverter energy losses of more than 60 percent under the tested conditions.
The inverter development used VisIC's D³GaN technology, NXP driver, AVL's PI850e Inverter Development Platform and AVL control software.
According to the company, integration into the vehicle demonstrator now enables the technology to be evaluated within a complete electric drivetrain environment and illustrates how the efficiency advantages of GaN can translate from semiconductor and inverter performance into vehicle-level benefits.
EV traction inverters operate across a wide range of speed, torque and load conditions. VisIC say its D³GaN technology is designed to combine low switching and conduction losses with high power density for high-power automotive applications.
The benefits can be particularly important during partial-load operation where reducing switching losses can improve inverter efficiency and reduce cooling requirements. Current 400V battery technology is especially attractive for PHEV and Range extended HEV cars. At vehicle level, this creates the potential for a more compact power-electronics system, improved drivetrain efficiency and increased driving range.
"Bringing D³GaN from the test bench into a fully operational vehicle is an important milestone for high-power GaN," said Tamara Baksht, VisIC Technologies' CEO. "The AVL demonstrator shows that GaN is no longer limited to discussing future potential. We can demonstrate the technology in the traction inverter of a real electric vehicle and show automotive manufacturers what higher efficiency, lower losses and higher power density can mean at system level."
"Integrating a GaN traction inverter into a vehicle demonstrator is an important step in understanding the opportunities and challenges of bringing this technology into future automotive applications," said Mathias Deiml, technical lead GaN Inverter Development, AVL Software and Functions. "The project combines semiconductor innovation with system-level development expertise and allows to push forward the state of the art regarding efficiency and advanced functionality."
The collaboration between AVL and VisIC Technologies is also intended to support the development of scalable GaN solutions for future EV architectures. The companies previously announced plans to extend the GaN-on-Silicon platform toward 800V GaN power modules, addressing the growing adoption of higher-voltage battery and drivetrain systems.

ETEL Announces Metis HP—A New High-Precision XY Air Bearing Stage for Step-and-Scan Semiconductor Applications
Heidenhain Corporation 
October 13, 2026 2 min read 
Heidenhain Corporation HEIDENHAIN Metis HP Stage 
HEIDENHAIN Metis HP Stage SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- ETEL , the leading supplier of high-performance motion control components and complete motion platforms, is proud to introduce the METIS HP, a new full air bearing planar platform designed for the most demanding step‑and‑scan semiconductor applications, including direct laser writing and high‑resolution optical inspection systems. With this new product, ETEL further strengthens its position as a leader in high-precision motion control by delivering a solution that combines exceptional speed and stability, outstanding dynamic straightness, and projected tool‑point measurement capability. 
"Building on ETEL's long‑standing expertise in high‑precision platforms, the METIS HP provides the trajectory quality required for advanced optical processes," said Stéphane Pellegrini, Product Manager at ETEL. "Its remarkable speed stability and dynamic straightness ensure consistent performance even at high scanning velocities. Supporting panel sizes up to 600 mm × 600 mm, the METIS HP addresses the growing need for next‑generation maskless lithography with large‑area substrates." 
At the core of the METIS HP is a multi‑degree‑of‑freedom (mDoF) HEIDENHAIN encoder, ensuring accuracy without thermal drift. This architecture enables projected tool‑point measurement. ETEL controllers can emulate a transistor-transistor logic (TTL) position signal for use as a trigger event. This innovative solution is a very compelling alternative to the classical interferometer used as an advanced trigger generator. With the METIS HP, there is no need for a mirror to be added on the carriage, no air lensing effect or air perturbation, and a lower cost. 
The METIS HP delivers outstanding performance, including ±150 nm accuracy over the full XY stroke after mapping, ±150 nm dynamic straightness at speeds up to 1 m/s, and dynamic capabilities reaching accelerations up to 20 m/s². These capabilities minimize turnaround time, thereby increasing machine throughput for step-and-scan applications. 
High-end inspection applications for advanced packaging require rapid and precise focal-distance adjustments. With its high-bandwidth 4-DoF module providing fine control over the Z, tip, tilt, and theta axes, METIS HP is the optimal platform for these demanding inspection tasks. 
The METIS HP is now available for OEM integration. For further information, visit ETEL's website at https://www.etel.ch/contact/ . Or visit ETEL at the HEIDENHAIN Booth 1639 during SEMICON West, taking place October 13-15, 2026, in San Francisco. 
Story Continues 
About ETEL S.A 
ETEL S.A., is part of HEIDENHAIN, located in Schaumburg, IL and Fremont, CA. As a leading international supplier of direct drive and motion control components and integrated systems, ETEL supports high tech industry with linear motors, torque motors, positioning stages, and motion controllers/systems. Mkango’s HyProMag USA Secures Power for Texas Rare Earth Magnet Hub
Abm

Mkango Magnetic Materials Ltd. (AIM/TSX-V: MKA) said HyProMag USA has secured power capacity with Oncor Electric Delivery Company for its planned Texas rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing hub.
The power allocation covers the initial cutting and finishing operation and the proposed Phase 1 development , with a pathway to additional capacity for Phase 2 through a substation upgrade.
HyProMag USA expects the electricity supplied to the facility to come predominantly from renewable energy sources .
PegasusTSI has started a contractor-selection process for the cutting and finishing facility, while Weston Solutions is progressing permitting activities.
The first stage is targeted for commissioning during the first half of 2027 .
That operation will not initially manufacture magnet blocks from recycled material in Texas. Instead, it is designed to cut, finish and qualify NdFeB magnet blocks supplied from other HyProMag Group operations .
The facility is intended to establish US finishing capability, customer qualification processes and workforce training ahead of the larger integrated development.
HyProMag USA plans to operate to recognised magnetic-material and quality standards, including ASTM A977/A977M and systems aligned with ISO 9001.
The larger Phase 1 Texas Hub is targeted for completion in mid-2028 . It is designed to produce approximately 550 tonnes per annum of sintered NdFeB magnet blocks and finished magnets , together with around 484 tonnes of co-products, giving approximately 1,034 tonnes per annum of total payable production .
A subsequent Phase 2 expansion envisages approximately 1,048 tonnes per annum of NdFeB magnet blocks and cylinders plus 478 tonnes of co-products, taking total payable production to approximately 1,526 tonnes per annum .
Importantly, those figures are design capacities rather than current production or confirmed future output .
CoTec chief executive Julian Treger said securing power, advancing permitting and commencing contractor selection further de-risk the project and support the goal of establishing a domestic US rare earth magnet supply chain.
For investors, the significance is that the Texas Hub is moving from engineering and planning towards site infrastructure, permitting and contractor procurement .
The next tangible milestones are the award of construction contracts, permitting progress and successful commissioning of the initial cutting and finishing operation in H1 2027 , followed by execution of the larger integrated Phase 1 development targeted for 2028.

CoTec Holdings Corp. Notes HyproMag USA Secures Power and Advances Project Readiness for Texas Rare Earth Magnet Recycling and Manufacturing Hub
Investing News Network 
October 13, 2026 
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / October 13, 2026 / CoTec Holdings Corp. ( TSXV:CTH )(OTCQX:CTHCF) ("CoTec" or the "Company") notes the press release issued today by its joint venture, HyProMag USA, LLC ("HyProMag USA"), providing an update on development activities for its Texas Hub rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing project in Dallas-Fort Worth, Texas (the "Texas Hub"). Following the commencement of formal power supply discussions announced on June 22, 2026, i HyProMag USA has secured electrical power capacity with Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC ("Oncor") for the Texas Hub development and expects the facility's electricity requirements to be supplied predominantly from renewable energy resources.
Key Highlights 
Power capacity secured: Power capacity secured with Oncor for both cutting and finishing operations and the Phase 1 development, with a pathway through a sub-station upgrade to provide power for Phase 2.
Contractor selection and permitting underway: Pegasus TSI, Inc. ("Pegasus") has commenced contractor selection for cutting and finishing operations and Weston Solutions, Inc. ("Weston") is advancing permitting activities.
Cutting and finishing operations targeted for H1 2027: Targeted commissioning of cutting and finishing operations in H1 2027 with the processing of neodymium iron boron ("NdFeB") magnet blocks, initially supplied from HyProMag Group operations, to produce finished magnets.
Phase 1 development: Phase 1 development is targeted for completion in mid-2028 and is designed to produce approximately 550 tonnes per annum ("tpa") of NdFeB magnet blocks and finished magnets and approximately 484 tpa of co-products, representing approximately 1,034 tpa of total payable production.
Phase 2 development: Phase 2 development envisions expansion to approximately 1,526 tpa of total payable production.
Renewable energy supply: Electricity supply expected to be sourced predominantly from renewable energy resources.
Julian Treger, Chief Executive Officer of CoTec Holdings Corp. , commented: "Securing power with Oncor, advancing permitting activities through Weston Solutions and commencing contractor selection are important milestones for the Texas Hub. Initial cutting and finishing operations in 2027 are expected to establish U.S. magnet finishing and qualification capabilities aligned with internationally recognized magnetic material and quality standards, while the full Phase 1 development will deliver integrated recycling and magnet manufacturing capacity. Together, these activities further de-risk the project and demonstrate continued progress towards establishing a domestic and sustainable rare earth magnet supply chain in the United States." 
Cutting and Finishing Operations 
Cutting and finishing operations in 2027 comprise the initial magnet finishing and qualification facility, enabling production and qualification of finished NdFeB magnets using magnet blocks supplied from HyProMag Group operations. The facility is designed to process NdFeB magnet blocks and support qualification of finished magnets in accordance with ASTM A977/A977M, the national classification standard for magnetic materials, together with quality management systems aligned with ISO 9001 and customer-specific quality, performance and traceability requirements. The objective is to establish qualification capabilities that meet the requirements of U.S. customers and establish a strategic training facility for the finishing of NdFeB magnets in advance of the main Texas Hub developments.
Permitting and Contractor Selection 
Weston is advancing permitting activities for the Texas Hub, while HyProMag USA's engineering partner Pegasus has commenced a Request for Quotation ("RFQ") process for the selection of a general contractor for cutting and finishing operations. Pegasus and BBA USA Inc. are HyProMag USA's U.S.-based engineering, procurement and construction management firms.
Phase 1 and Phase 2 Development 
Phase 1 represents the first integrated recycling and magnet manufacturing stage of the Texas Hub and is designed to produce approximately 550 tpa of sintered NdFeB magnet blocks and finished magnets, together with approximately 484 tpa of co-products, representing total payable production of approximately 1,034 tpa. Upon completion of Phase 2, the Texas Hub is expected to produce approximately 1,048 tpa of sintered NdFeB magnet blocks and cylinders, together with approximately 478 tpa of co-products, representing total payable production of approximately 1,526 tpa.
About HyProMag USA 
HyProMag USA is developing advanced rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing operations to establish a secure domestic U.S. supply chain for NdFeB magnets, essential components for AI infrastructure, defense systems, robotics, electric vehicles, and advanced electronics. Leveraging the revolutionary Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap ("HPMS") technology, developed over 15 years with over US$100 million in R&D investment, HyProMag USA delivers faster magnet-to-magnet short-loop recycling that uses 88% less energy and reduces carbon emissions by 85% compared to conventional methods. HPMS accepts a wide range of magnet-bearing feedstocks - including end-of-life EV motors, data-center and industrial equipment, consumer electronics, and manufacturing scrap - enabling recovery of magnet-grade material without chemical processing.
Ownership 
HyProMag USA LLC is owned 50:50 by CoTec and HyProMag Limited. HyProMag Limited is 100% owned by Maginito Limited, which is owned 79.4% by Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited (AIM/TSX-V: MKA) and 20.6% by CoTec.
For more information on HyProMag USA, please visit www.hypromagusa.com 
About CoTec 
CoTec Holdings Corp. ( TSXV:CTH )(OTCQX:CTHCF) is redefining the future of resource extraction and recycling. Focused on rare earth magnets and strategic materials, CoTec integrates breakthrough technologies with strategic assets to unlock secure, sustainable, and low-cost supply chains.
CoTec's mission is clear: accelerate the energy transition while strengthening strategic mineral supply chains for the countries we operate in. By investing in and deploying disruptive technologies, the Company delivers capital-efficient, scalable solutions that transform marginal assets, tailings, waste streams, and recycled products into high-value critical minerals.
From its HyProMag USA magnet recycling joint venture in Texas, to iron tailings reprocessing and reclamation in Québec, to next-generation copper and iron solutions backed by global majors, CoTec is building a diversified portfolio with long-term growth, rapid cash flow potential, and high barriers to entry. The result is a differentiated platform at the intersection of technology, sustainability, and strategic materials.

Vestas Completes Taiwan's First V236-15.0 MW™ Offshore Wind Turbine Hub Assembly Ahead of Schedule; Achieves Milestone in CIP's Fengmiao 1 Project
Oct. 13 2026
Vestas Completes Taiwan's First V236-15.0 MW™ Offshore Wind Turbine Hub Assembly Ahead of Schedule; Achieves Milestone in CIP's Fengmiao 1 Project
Share
Vestas has completed the assembly of Taiwan's first V236-15.0 MW™ offshore wind turbine hub , marking a milestone in the introduction of next-generation offshore wind technology to Taiwan. The achievement was supported by steady progress on the CIP's 495 MW Fengmiao 1 Offshore Wind Farm (渢妙一期) , the first project in Taiwan's Round 3 offshore wind zonal development to secure full financing and commence construction.
Since entering Taiwan in 2000, Vestas has established a strong presence in both onshore and offshore wind, employing more than 500 people locally. The successful assembly combined the company's global technological expertise with the capabilities of its Taiwan team, which has developed specialized skills in quality management, testing and safety procedures for critical turbine components. The hub was delivered ahead of schedule, with safety and quality remaining top priorities.
Vestas Asia-Pacific President Purvin Patel said, "Completing Taiwan's first V236 hub assembly is an important milestone for Vestas. It demonstrates that our Taiwan team can deliver safely, to a high standard of quality and on schedule. The skills and experience gained through this work will also serve as an important foundation for the continued development of Taiwan's offshore wind industry."
The V236-15.0 MW™ is Vestas' flagship offshore wind turbine platform, designed to support standardized, large-scale production and improve project execution efficiency. Upon completion of Fengmiao 1, Vestas' cumulative offshore wind capacity delivered in Taiwan is expected to reach approximately 1.7 GW, reinforcing the company's long-term commitment to Taiwan's offshore wind sector and its contribution to the country's energy security.
【About Vestas】 
Vestas is a global leader in sustainable energy solutions, specializing in the design, manufacturing, installation, and servicing of onshore and offshore wind turbines. The company has installed more than 207 GW of wind power capacity across 88 countries worldwide and currently services wind turbines with a combined capacity of more than 165 GW. 
Leveraging industry-leading data analytics capabilities and a global service network, Vestas continues to deliver efficient and reliable wind energy solutions to its customers. With more than 36,000 employees worldwide, Vestas is committed to advancing energy security and building a more sustainable future.

Asahi Kasei Acquisition Pays Off With FDA Approval for Novel Herpes Drug 
Asahi Kasei’s Hovilpri is now approved for treating lesions caused by herpes simplex virus infection. This daily pill came from the $919 million acquisition of AiCuris Anti-Infective Cures.
By Frank Vinluan on October 12, 2026 10:44 am 
Share 
Share Options 
Share a link to this article
Copy Link 
Copy Link 
Email 
Facebook 
LinkedIn 
X 
Patients with lesions caused by herpes simplex virus have a new FDA-approved treatment option, an oral antiviral drug from Asahi Kasei.
The late Friday regulatory decision covers the treatment of adults whose lesions do not respond to the three oral antivirals that make up the current standard of care. Asahi Kasei’s once-daily pill, known in development as pritelivir, will be commercialized under the brand name Hovilpri.
In people with healthy immune systems, herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection is often asymptomatic or causes mild disease. But in people with weakened immune symptoms — those who have undergone a transplant procedure, or patients with HIV, cancer, or autoimmune disorders — HSV infection can occur more frequently and with greater severity. While oral antivirals are available to treat HSV, viral mutations can lead to resistance to these older drugs. There are alternative treatment options, but they require intravenous dosing.
Sponsored Post 
The Power Behind Enterprise EHR Software for Large Healthcare Systems  
Enterprise EHR boosts scalability, interoperability, and governance for large healthcare systems. 
By Malvika Tarnekar, Director of Product Strategy, PrognoCIS by Bizmatics Inc 
Hovilpri gives patients the choice of an oral drug with a different mechanism of action. This small molecule is designed to inhibit a complex of enzymes key to the synthesis of viral DNA. The drug was developed to treat both types of HSV, HSV-1 and HSV-2.
The regulatory submission for Hovilpri was based on the results of a Phase 3 study that showed statistically significant superiority in lesion healing up to day 28 compared to the physician’s choice of treatment. The most common adverse reaction reported for the study drug was headache.
“Today’s approval delivers the first FDA-approved treatment for refractory mucocutaneous HSV lesions with a novel mechanism of action in nearly 30 years and marks an important advancement for immunocompromised adults,” Stacy Wheeler, CEO of Asahi Kasei Therapeutics in the U.S. and Europe, said in a prepared statement. “Hovilpri offers a new oral treatment option for adult patients with a persistent, difficult-to-treat disease.”
Hovilpri was originally developed by AiCuris Anti-Infective Cures, a Germany-based biopharmaceutical company acquired by Asahi Kasei for €780 million (about $919 million). In the February acquisition announcement, Tokyo-based Asahi Kasei said the deal strengthens the company’s presence in severe infectious disease. It added that HSV patients addressed by Hovilpri are commonly seen in transplant centers and specialized hospital settings where the company has established commercial relationships and infrastructure.
Sponsored Post 
The Hidden Administrative Tasks Draining Small Practices 
Small practices play a critical role in healthcare delivery, but they cannot continue to absorb ever-increasing administrative demands without consequences. 
By Michael Blackman, MD, MBA Chief Medical Officer, Greenway Health® 
Asahi Kasei has been expanding its portfolio and pipeline via business deals. In 2020, the company closed the 8.3 billion Danish krone (about $1.3 billion) acquisition of Veloxis Pharmaceuticals , a company that develops and sells therapies for organ transplant patients. The Japanese company’s 11.8 billion Swedish krona (about $1.18 billion) acquisition of Calliditas Pharmaceuticals in 2024 brought a portfolio that includes Tarpeyo, which has FDA approval for treating the rare kidney disorder immunoglobulin A nephropathy.
The Aicuris acquisition brought more than Hovilpri. Asahi Kasei gains royalty income from Prevymis, a cytomegalovirus drug whose global rights Aicuris had licensed to Merck. The Japanese company also gets an experimental antisense oligonucleotide that Aicuris has advanced to Phase 1 testing as a treatment for BK virus infection in kidney transplant patients.

ARKAY has announced the inauguration of a next-generation acrylic acid purification unit at its Carling site in France, strengthening its competitive position in Europe's market while advancing decarbonization. The nearly 150 million Euro investment is one of the company's largest industrial projects in France and contributes to its ambitious climate investment program. 
The new unit improves the energy efficiency of the purification process by 25% and reduces the carbon intensity of the Carling site by 20%. Its innovative technology also optimizes resource and waste management while significantly lowering solvent consumption. These improvements enhance efficiency to reinforce Arkema's position in the low-carbon acrylic materials market. 
The Carling facility is a leading acrylic production site, manufacturing acrylic monomers used in performance coatings, adhesives, water treatment and other advanced materials. The project, decided in 2023, received partial funding from the French State under the France 2030 program, operated by ADEME, and from the European Union's NextGenerationEU initiative. 
The cumulative investments could reach €400 million over 2022-2030, under the company's decarbonization plans, while making its industrial hubs the driving forces of future. Arkema's investment also aligns with its strategy to strengthen its Specialty Materials segment and its increasing focus on reducing emissions across the industry.

title: Aicuris acquisition delivers new drug for Asahi Kasei - pharmaphorum
query: "Asahi Kasei" ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Aicuris acquisition delivers new drug for Asahi Kasei
News
Asahi Kasei's $920 million takeover of German biotech Aicuris in April has paid off with FDA approval for the herpes simplex virus (HSV) drug at the heart of the deal. 
The oral drug, called Hovilpri (pritelivir), has been cleared for treating adults with weakened immune systems who have sores on the skin or mucous membranes – such as lips, nostrils, eyes, and genitals – that are caused by HSV and have not responded to standard nucleoside analogue therapies like acyclovir, valacyclovir, or famciclovir.
Hovilpri, which acts as a helicase-primase inhibitor, represents the first FDA approved HSV therapy with a novel mechanism of action in nearly 30 years, according to Asahi Kasei. It also provides an oral alternative to intravenously administered antivirals used to treat immunocompromised adults with refractory HSV infection, with or without resistance to current drugs.
There are two types of HSV infection – HSV-1 and HSV-2 – which cause common infections like cold sores and genital herpes. Most people are exposed to the virus in childhood and recover from the primary infection, although in many cases the virus lies dormant.
HSV is a major threat to immunocompromised people, as the virus can quickly reactivate and cause lesions that release contagious virus particles.
The FDA approval of Hovilpri draws on the pivotal, open-label PRIOH-1 study, which enrolled 101 immunocompromised adults and compared the drug with investigator's choice of available treatments for up to 28 days until all mucocutaneous lesions healed, which was extended up to 42 days if lesions were improving, but not completely healed, after 28 days.
The primary endpoint was the proportion of participants with all lesions healed during the treatment period up to 28 days, which was achieved in 63% of patients receiving Hovilpri, compared with 34% of patients receiving one of the other medications.
The study recruited adults who had weakened immunity due to a wide range of causes, including haematopoietic stem cell transplants (HSCT) for serious illnesses, various forms of cancer, HIV infection, autoimmune diseases, and solid organ transplantation.
Asahi Kasei said that it expects to launch Hovilpri in the US before the end of the year, but has not released pricing details as yet.
Aicuris , which now operates as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Asahi Kasei, previously developed another antiviral used for HSCT patients, MSD-marketed Prevymis (letermovir), which is used to prevent infection with cytomegalovirus (CMV).
It is also developing AIC468, which aims to prevent and treat BK virus infections in kidney transplant recipients.
Asahi Kasei has a long history in the anti-infectives arena, with products like antifungal Cresemba (isavuconazonium sulfate) and aminoglycoside antibiotic Exacin (isepamicin), and has said that adding Aicuris will help it reach its goal of driving pharma sales to around $1.9 billion) by its 2030 fiscal year.
Image
Phil Taylor

Renishaw completes first phase of £70m Welsh manufacturing site expansion 
Posted on 12 Oct 2026 by James Devonshire 
Share this article: 
Share on Linkedin 
Share on Twitter 
Share on facebook 
Copy Link 
Company: 
Renishaw 
Engineering technologies business Renishaw has completed the first phase of a £70m expansion at its Miskin facility in South Wales, increasing manufacturing capacity to meet rising demand for its precision measurement and additive manufacturing technologies. 
The development, first announced in 2022, forms part of a long-term investment programme that will ultimately double the size of the site, west of Cardiff, establishing it as one of the UK’s largest advanced manufacturing facilities.
The completion of Hall 3 has increased the site’s usable space to 617,000 sq ft (57,350 sqm). Once Hall 4 is completed and operational, the facility will cover 880,000 sq ft (81,765 sqm). The expansion coincides with the 15th anniversary of Renishaw’s acquisition of the 193-acre site from Robert Bosch Ltd in September 2011. From an initial operation employing around 25 people when the facility officially opened in October 2012, the site now employs approximately 950.
Renishaw has invested around £150m at Miskin to date, covering the site acquisition, refurbishment of existing buildings, new construction and the installation of advanced manufacturing equipment.
Meeting demand for advanced manufacturing technologies 
The latest development will help Renishaw increase production of its precision metrology, additive manufacturing and position measurement products, with growing demand for semiconductor manufacturing equipment creating an immediate requirement for additional capacity.
Hall 3 houses manufacturing operations for the company’s metal additive manufacturing (AM) systems and AGILITY co-ordinate measuring machines (CMMs), alongside a multimillion-pound automated storage and retrieval warehousing system.
Hall 4 was initially constructed as a shell building, allowing Renishaw to bring the space into use as customer demand and production requirements evolved. Exceptional demand for the company’s position encoders, driven by the growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), means part of the building will now be occupied over the coming months.
The Miskin facility currently operates 134 CNC machine tools, producing around one million parts per month, alongside three printed circuit board (PCB) assembly lines, robotic assembly systems and automated warehousing. Further equipment is on order to support customer requirements.
Our long-term commitment to manufacturing is exemplified by the investment that we have made in Miskin over the past 15 years and I would like to thank the many people from across our business who have supported the development of this world-class facility.
Jim Long, Director of Group Manufacturing at Renishaw 
Sustainability and workforce investment 
The expansion has also been designed to improve the facility’s environmental performance. Both new halls have been designed to achieve Net Zero Carbon in Operation, supporting Renishaw’s commitment to reaching Net Zero greenhouse gas emissions across Scopes 1 and 2 by 2028. The company’s longer-term ambition is for all buildings at Miskin to operate at Net Zero.
Alongside the manufacturing investment, Renishaw has developed an employee wellbeing centre incorporating a restaurant and fitness suite. Improvements to the wider site include landscaped outdoor spaces, picnic areas and a 2km perimeter walking route.
The investment underlines Renishaw’s commitment to South Wales, with additional manufacturing space intended to support future growth in demand for advanced engineering technologies.
“The significant ongoing investment by our Board to increase our production capabilities demonstrates a huge vote of confidence in our manufacturing operations and people, at an exciting time for the business,” Long added.

Exclusive   ​ASML to Raise Lithography Spare Parts Prices

ASML, the world's largest semiconductor equipment maker, will raise prices by 10% across replacement parts supplied to South Korea.
​The increase covers all parts for extreme ultraviolet (EUV) and deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography systems. The new prices will take effect for deliveries starting in January 2027.
​ASML headquarters notified Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix of the proposed increase through its South Korean subsidiary in early September, according to industry sources. The increase was finalized after discussions with the purchasing organizations of both companies.
​Prices will rise for everything from consumable parts purchased regularly to major components replaced because of failures or performance degradation. Lithography systems contain numerous components, including optical parts such as lenses and mirrors that direct light, light sources and precision motion-control systems. The increase will raise the cost of keeping the equipment operational.
​ASML has traditionally adjusted prices for individual parts when raw material costs rose sharply or specific materials became difficult to procure, according to industry sources. A blanket 10% increase is unusual.
​"Prices have risen across the board for the components that make up these parts, but ASML also appears to be seeking a larger share of the profits its customers are making," an industry official said.
​ASML separately reports revenue from services, parts and upgrades for equipment already installed at customer sites. This revenue totaled €8.193 billion last year, accounting for 25% of total sales of €32.667 billion. ASML forecast that revenue from this business would grow by more than 30% this year.
​Prices for newly ordered ASML equipment are also likely to increase, following the spare-parts hike. The company is discussing equipment price increases with major customers.
​The Information, a US technology news outlet, reported in July that ASML had notified Chinese semiconductor manufacturers and other customers of a 10% increase in DUV equipment prices, with some customers accepting the change. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), ASML's largest customer, was reportedly opposing the increase.
​Industry observers expect ASML's decision to raise prices across the board, accepted by Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, to strengthen the position of other semiconductor equipment and component suppliers seeking price increases.
​Price hikes are already under way. US-based Applied Materials said during its earnings announcement in August that prices had risen for both new and existing products. Japan's Tokyo Electron also said at an earnings briefing in late July that it was pursuing price adjustments, including for equipment already on the market, to offset rising costs. US plasma power supply maker Advanced Energy Industries likewise said it had raised prices for some product lines.
​The broader price increases reflect a supply-demand imbalance. Investment in artificial intelligence (AI) data centers has prompted memory makers and foundries to expand capacity simultaneously, driving up orders for equipment and components. Suppliers need time to expand their facilities and increase production. Rising inflation and raw material costs have also added to their cost burdens. Unlike in the past, when semiconductor manufacturers used their purchasing power to demand lower prices, suppliers now have greater leverage in negotiations.
​"Large-scale capacity expansion is translating into actual demand, pushing equipment and components into a supply-shortage phase," an industry official said. "As wafer input volumes increase, the materials used in production will also face large-scale supply shortages."

title: Samsung's HBM Market Share Jumps to 33%; Hybrid Bonding Technology Could Be Key to Overtaking Rivals - BigGo Finance
query: "Tokyo Electron" ("hybrid bonding" OR "wafer bonding" OR "advanced packaging" OR "bonding equipment" OR "die bonding" OR "semiconductor packaging") after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
discovery_snippet: Samsung's HBM Market Share Jumps to 33%; Hybrid Bonding Technology Could Be Key to Overtaking Rivals    BigGo Finance
content_text:
Samsung's HBM Market Share Jumps to 33%; Hybrid Bonding Technology Could Be Key to Overtaking Rivals
Add preferred source 3 
Samsung Electronics' share of the HBM market surged from 21% in Q1 2026 to 33% in Q2, while SK Hynix retained the top spot with a 50% revenue share, down from 58% in the prior quarter. Separately, an expert interview report indicates Samsung has begun delivering HBM samples using hybrid bonding technology to customers, while SK Hynix is reportedly encountering difficulties in developing the same technology. SK Hynix, however, continues to advance sample deliveries of 12-layer HBM4E using its existing Advanced MR-MUF packaging technology. Hybrid bonding faces significant manufacturing challenges including chemical mechanical polishing, surface contamination, and die warpage — the gap from samples to mass production remains substantial. HBM competition is shifting from simply increasing stack layers toward a systemic contest spanning memory design, bonding processes, thermal management, and advanced packaging.
Key Elements 
Samsung Electronics SK Hynix HBM Hybrid Bonding Advanced MR-MUF Micron Nvidia Applied Materials Besi Counterpoint Research Tokyo Electron DISCO TSMC imec 
In the competitive landscape for high-bandwidth memory (HBM), Samsung Electronics is pressuring long-time leader SK Hynix from two directions simultaneously: rapid market share gains and an early advantage in validating next-generation advanced packaging technology. According to an expert interview published by semiconductor research newsletter Damnang Research on October 6, SK Hynix is encountering difficulties in developing hybrid bonding technology for next-generation HBM, while Samsung Electronics is reportedly already delivering samples using the technology to customers. The interview was conducted on September 19 with a process development engineer from SK Hynix's Future Technology Research Institute; the interview notes state that the content reflects the interviewee's personal views and does not represent the company's position, with the full transcript behind a paywall.
If confirmed, this would mean Samsung is positioned to complete customer validation first in advanced packaging — a critical process that will determine future HBM competitiveness. However, the information did not come from official announcements by either company, and the report did not specify the HBM generation, stack count, or customer details involved. It is therefore premature to assess the actual R&D gap between the two companies, let alone conclude that Samsung has taken a comprehensive lead in next-generation HBM competition.
Notably, SK Hynix's progress on hybrid bonding technology is not equivalent to its next-generation HBM product development timeline. As early as June 18, SK Hynix announced it had delivered 12-layer HBM4E samples to major customers, with 48GB capacity, using its existing Advanced MR-MUF packaging technology. The company said the product achieves a 17% improvement in thermal resistance compared to HBM4. This means that even if hybrid bonding development faces headwinds, SK Hynix is still advancing next-generation HBM products along its existing packaging route.
The real question worth examining: as HBM moves toward higher stack counts, how far can traditional packaging processes meet performance, thermal, and package-height requirements — and what manufacturing hurdles must hybrid bonding clear before it can reach volume production?
Two Technology Routes Diverge
HBM provides high-bandwidth memory for GPUs and AI accelerators by vertically stacking multiple DRAM dies. As AI models continue to grow in scale, HBM must not only increase capacity and bandwidth but also manage power consumption and heat generation within constrained package space.
▲ Basic HBM structure: multiple DRAM dies vertically stacked via through-silicon vias (TSV) and micro bumps, connected to the GPU through a silicon interposer (early-generation schematic shown). Hybrid bonding aims to replace the micro bumps and fill materials at the bonding interface. (Image source: Wikimedia Commons, author ScotXW, CC BY-SA 4.0) 
Currently, traditional HBM stacking typically uses micro bumps to connect upper and lower dies, with fill and protection material processes handling the gaps between dies. SK Hynix's Advanced MR-MUF represents this technology route, improving the reliability and thermal performance of the stacked structure by optimizing micro bump connections and the filling and curing processes for liquid protective materials.
Hybrid bonding, by contrast, seeks to further reduce reliance on micro bumps. The technology directly connects copper interconnect structures on the surfaces of upper and lower dies while simultaneously bonding the surrounding dielectric insulation layers, thereby reducing the space occupied by traditional interconnect structures. Its advantages: smaller interconnect pitch and shorter electrical connection distances, which can improve interconnect density, reduce signal transmission loss, and create conditions for higher-density DRAM stacking. Reducing some intermediate materials at the bonding interface may also improve thermal conduction.
As HBM moves from 12 layers toward 16 layers and beyond, space constraints between dies and thermal pressure will become more pronounced, raising the potential value of hybrid bonding.
Samsung introduced its hybrid copper bonding technology, HCB, on March 17 in a presentation tied to GTC-related activities, positioning it as a technology solution supporting next-generation HBM with 16 or more layers. Samsung said HCB is expected to reduce thermal resistance by more than 20% compared to traditional thermocompression bonding (TCB). This technology direction aligns with the sample progress reported in the interview, but a technology demonstration does not equate to volume production.
It should be noted that Samsung's published thermal resistance improvement cannot be directly ranked against SK Hynix's 17% improvement for HBM4E versus the previous generation: the former compares bonding methods, while the latter compares products across generations — the comparison baselines are fundamentally different.
Looking at the three publicly disclosed developments together, each differs in subject, methodology, and stage:
Announcer & Date Subject & Method Disclosed Progress How to Read the Numbers 
Samsung Electronics, March 17, 2026 (GTC) Hybrid copper bonding technology HCB for next-gen HBM with 16+ layers Introduced bonding technology Thermal resistance reduced 20%+ vs. traditional TCB; a technology showcase, not a volume production or customer qualification announcement 
SK Hynix, June 18, 2026 12-layer, 48GB HBM4E using Advanced MR-MUF Delivered samples to major customers Thermal resistance improved 17% vs. previous-gen HBM4; this product does not use hybrid bonding 
imec & EV Group, May 28, 2026 (ECTC) Wafer-to-wafer (W2W) hybrid bonding test structures 200nm copper pad pitch; post-bond overlay error below 40nm for all dies on 300mm wafers Research institution results on test structures, not HBM volume production performance 
Note: The three disclosures differ in subject, methodology, and stage; the numbers cannot be directly compared across them.
The Gap from Lab to Mass Production
The manufacturing difficulty of hybrid bonding extends far beyond precisely aligning and joining two dies.
According to process explanations from Applied Materials, chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) is one of the critical steps. Manufacturers must precisely control the height relationship between copper pads and the surrounding dielectric layer to achieve nanometer-level flatness on the bonding surface. If the copper surface is recessed too deeply, the upper and lower copper structures may fail to make adequate contact; if the copper protrudes excessively, it may interfere with dielectric bonding and increase the risk of interface defects. Therefore, bonding surface flatness, copper pad height, and consistency across the entire area must all be tightly controlled.
At the same time, particles generated during polishing and die singulation, surface contamination, and changes in surface properties over time after activation can all affect bonding quality. This requires manufacturers to coordinate cleaning, surface treatment, environmental cleanliness, and bonding time windows. In other words, hybrid bonding is not a problem that can be solved by purchasing a single high-precision bonding tool. Polishing, cleaning, inspection, die alignment, and bonding must form a stable process chain to convert successful lab-scale bonding into repeatable volume production results.
HBM's structural characteristics further compound the difficulty. To increase stack counts while controlling package height, DRAM dies must be continuously thinned. But the thinner the die, the more susceptible it is to mechanical stress-induced warpage, which in turn increases the risk of positional misalignment and bonding defects. As stack counts rise, multiple bonding interfaces also mean more potential failure points.
However, there is currently no reliable information indicating which specific process step is causing difficulties for SK Hynix. CMP, surface contamination, and die warpage are manufacturing challenges common to hybrid bonding and cannot be directly assumed to be the cause of the reported development hurdles.
The industrialization of hybrid bonding also depends on the specific die bonding approach. imec has previously demonstrated wafer-to-wafer (W2W) bonding, where two entire wafers are aligned and bonded together. This approach can process large numbers of dies at once, but if defective dies are bonded along with good ones, overall yield may suffer. The alternative is die-to-wafer (D2W) bonding, where known-good dies are first screened and then individually placed onto a target wafer for bonding. Its advantage is the ability to prioritize tested good dies, but picking, positioning, and bonding dies one by one introduces production efficiency challenges.
An analysis by Inha University professor Seunghwan Joo, published on SK Hynix's newsroom, noted that die-to-wafer bonding is moving toward HBM commercialization. This illustrates that the bonding precision demonstrated in wafer-level experiments is not the same problem as the yield and production efficiency required for multi-layer HBM stacking.
Equipment vendors are also refining the process chain around this manufacturing challenge. On October 1, Applied Materials and Besi announced an expansion of their collaboration in advanced packaging. The two companies are combining Applied Materials' process technologies in polishing, cleaning, and metrology with Besi's die placement and bonding technology, with one outcome being the Kinex integrated die-to-wafer hybrid bonding system. This collaboration reflects how hybrid bonding competition is extending from the precision of individual tools to process integration capabilities before and after bonding. However, existing information does not indicate that Samsung or SK Hynix has adopted this system.
Japanese equipment makers also hold a position in this process chain. DRAM dies must undergo grinding and thinning before stacking, placing Japanese equipment maker DISCO's thinning, grinding, and dicing tools at a critical front-end position in HBM manufacturing — by various estimates, the company holds roughly 70-80% global share in dicing equipment and about 60-70% in thinning and grinding equipment. DISCO said that for the die-to-wafer (D2W) process required by hybrid bonding, the company has prepared multiple solutions including plasma dicing, dicing-before-grinding (DBG), and laser dicing; while cleanliness management is more difficult than conventional dicing, it is "not particularly demanding compared to front-end processes." Tokyo Electron has already launched bonding equipment for wafer-to-wafer (W2W) applications and is developing D2W bonding technology, with strong demand for its HBM-related equipment.
In the logic chip space, hybrid bonding has already entered volume production: TSMC's SoIC (System on Integrated Chips) uses copper-to-copper hybrid bonding and has been applied to AMD's 3D V-Cache stacking (Ryzen X3D series processors) since 2022, as confirmed by teardown reports from packaging analysis firm TechInsights. The difference lies in the application context — that involves bonding a single cache die to a compute die, whereas HBM must accommodate more than ten layers of ultra-thin DRAM within a constrained package height while simultaneously meeting yield, capacity, and cost requirements.
For HBM manufacturers, the real challenge is keeping every bonding interface stable, meeting product reliability requirements after multi-layer stacking, and keeping production efficiency and manufacturing costs within acceptable ranges. Successfully bonding samples is only the first step.
Substantive Changes in Market Share
Behind the technology route debate, Samsung's share of the HBM market is undergoing substantive change.
According to Counterpoint Research data, Samsung's HBM revenue share rose from 21% in Q1 2026 to 33% in Q2; SK Hynix retained the top spot with a 50% revenue share, but that was down 8 percentage points from 58% in Q1, with its lead narrowing significantly; Micron ranked third at 18%, down slightly from 21% in Q1. For context, SK Hynix's share was as high as 64% in Q2 2025. Samsung announced in February 2026 that it had begun volume shipments of HBM4 (claiming to be the industry's first) and said its 2026 HBM sales are expected to more than triple versus 2025.
Vendor Q1 2026 Q2 2026 QoQ Change Q2 2025 (Reference) 
SK Hynix 58% 50% -8 ppt 64% 
Samsung Electronics 21% 33% +12 ppt — 
Micron 21% 18% -3 ppt — 
Note: All figures are revenue share basis; QoQ refers to Q2 2026 versus Q1 2026.
Market expectations are that Samsung's share will expand further as HBM4 shipments increase in the second half of the year. According to KB Securities data, HBM4 products are expected to account for 80% of Samsung's HBM sales by 2027, doubling from 40% this year. The market also expects Samsung's HBM product prices to more than double by 2027 versus this year, with its product contract prices the highest among the three major memory makers including SK Hynix and Micron.
From a broader perspective, HBM competition is shifting from simply increasing stack layers toward a systemic contest spanning memory design, bonding processes, thermal management, and advanced packaging. Hybrid bonding holds the potential to further unlock the possibilities of high-density stacking, but what ultimately determines its industrial value is not whether a batch of samples can be successfully produced, but whether technological advantages can be converted into sustained delivery capability through stable yields, reasonable costs, and sufficient capacity.
If the information in this report is accurate — that Samsung has delivered hybrid bonding HBM samples to customers — then its advantage lies primarily in the R&D and customer validation timeline. Entering customer testing earlier helps identify bonding reliability, thermal, and system integration issues sooner, accumulating experience for subsequent product development. But there remains a distance between sample delivery and volume production. Customer qualification progress, mass production yields, manufacturing costs, and available supply scale are the key metrics for judging whether a technological advantage can translate into commercial competitiveness.
At the same time, SK Hynix has advanced HBM4E sample deliveries through Advanced MR-MUF, demonstrating that the traditional packaging route still has a role to play. New hybrid bonding does not mean existing processes will exit the market immediately; the two routes can develop in parallel, with specific choices depending on product performance requirements, manufacturing capabilities, and volume production economics.
In the next phase, what deserves closer attention is at which HBM generation and stack count each company introduces hybrid bonding, and whether substantive differences emerge in customer qualification, volume production timelines, and yield performance.

09-Oct-2026

Arkema continues to invest in the battery business value chain and announces a €10 million expansion project for its Global Battery Center of Excellence located in Oullins-Pierre-Bénite, in the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region of France.
Arkema
This investment reflects the Group’s strategy of continuously strengthening its research capabilities in advanced materials for batteries within its global network of R &D laboratories covering the entire battery value chain.
Following the inauguration in Normandy in September 2025 of a laboratory dedicated to solvent-free battery electrode manufacturing , as well as several investments in Asia and the Americas, this expansion further strengthens a particularly dense global R&D network, that combines the expertise developed in France with that of the Group’s research centers in China, South Korea, Japan and the United States. Thanks to this international organization, Arkema is accelerating the development of innovative solutions capable of addressing the technological and industrial challenges of next- generation batteries.
Located at the heart of the Rhône-Alpes Research Center , the Battery Center of Excellence is entering a new phase of its development. Its footprint will be tripled, and its research infrastructure will be modernized, including notably a significant increase in the digitalization of R&D activities. This expansion will consolidate the role of this French center as Arkema’s global reference platform for the development of advanced materials serving both current batteries and the next generations under development.
The project will enable the Group’s R&D teams to prepare for the future industrial standards of cell manufacturers and accelerate the integration of Arkema’s advanced materials into their production processes. By replicating their customers’ manufacturing conditions, researchers will be able to better anticipate implementation constraints and contribute to the development of more efficient batteries delivering greater energy density, faster charging times and enhanced safety.
Armand Ajdari, Arkema’s Chief technology Officer: "This investment marks a major milestone in Arkema’s ambition to support the rapid evolution of the battery market. By strengthening our Battery Center of Excellence in France, we are equipping our global network and teams with state-of-the-art tools that will enable them to develop, in close collaboration with our customers, the materials that will contribute to the performance of tomorrow’s batteries."
The implementation of this project has been made possible in particular through the support provided by the French Research Tax Credit ( Crédit d’Impôt Recherche ) and by the French State as part of the France 2030 program.

title: Arkema inaugurates its next-generation acrylic acid purification unit in Carling - Arkema Global
query: "Arkema" ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Arkema inaugurates its next-generation acrylic acid purification unit in Carling
Download the PDF 
Arkema has inaugurated a new acrylic acid purification unit featuring an innovative process at its Carling site in France. This facility positions the Group among the most competitive players in Europe and contributes to the decarbonization of the European chemical industry. It is part of Arkema’s decarbonization investment program and supports the implementation of its ambitious climate plan.
The inauguration ceremony for the new unit was held in the presence of Thierry Le Hénaff, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Arkema and Stéphane Séjourné, Executive Vice-President of the European Commission for Prosperity and Industrial Strategy.
The ceremony took place on the same day as the Critical Chemicals Alliance General Assembly, which brought together European industrial leaders and policy-makers to discuss the key challenges of sovereignty, competitiveness, and decarbonization.
With an investment of nearly €150 million, this new unit represents one of Arkema’s largest industrial projects in France.
It will contribute to the Group’s ambitious climate plan, underpinned by a dedicated investment program supporting Arkema’s decarbonization, with a cumulative amount that could reach €400 million over the 2022-2030 period.” 
Thierry Le Hénaff, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Arkema.
“Europe must keep its chemical industry. There can be neither industrial sovereignty nor strategic autonomy if we allow the essential building blocks of our economy to leave. Carling is showing the way forward: nearly €150 million invested to produce in Europe, using less energy and generating less carbon, while building on decades of industrial know-how. This is exactly the model we want to promote: decarbonizing without deindustrializing, investing in our regions, and making our industrial hubs the driving forces of our future.” 
Stéphane Séjourné, Executive Vice-President of the European Commission for Prosperity and Industrial Strategy. 
The Carling site is one of the leading acrylic production facilities in Europe. It produces acrylic monomer s used in performance coatings, adhesives, water treatment and other advanced materials.
The new unit improves the energy efficiency of the purification process by 25% and reduces the carbon intensity of the site’s operations by 20%. The innovative technology deployed also helps optimize resource and waste management while significantly reducing solvent consumption.
Thanks to this investment, the Carling plant is positioning itself among the reference sites in the industry, aligned with the highest operational and environmental standards . It also strengthens Arkema’s leadership in the low-carbon acrylic materials market.
This project has been decided in 2023 and has been partly funded by the French State as part of the France 2030 program, operated by ADEME, and funded by the European Union – NextGenerationEU.
